definition_en: a device of connected parts that performs work; also a computer or an organised system, and to cut or shape with a machine tool
core_image: 一台车床夹着一段金属，刀头沿着导轨推进，铁屑卷成一圈圈落下来
scene: 车间的车床夹着一段金属，刀头沿导轨推进，铁屑卷成一圈圈落下。The machine cut the shaft to within a hair of the required size.
sceneCN: 这里 machine 指由部件组成并做功的装置（第 1 个义项：机器这一装置）；句意：这台机器把轴削到与要求尺寸相差不到一根头发。

pos.zh: 机器；计算机；运作体系
用机床加工；机械切削

senses.title: A device that performs work
senses.definition: an assembly of connected parts that uses power to carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 由相连部件构成、使用动力完成任务的组合体
senses.example: The machine lifts the load with a single lever.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只用一个手柄就抬起货物。
senses.why: the Greek noun named any contrivance, so the first sense is the broad one of a built device.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词原指任何巧妙装置，因此第一个义项就是「人造装置」这一宽泛含义。

senses.title: A computer
senses.definition: the computing hardware that executes stored instructions
senses.definitionCN: 执行已存指令的计算硬件
senses.example: The machine rebooted before the backup finished.
senses.exampleCN: 备份还没完成，机器就重启了。
senses.why: computers became the most common machine in daily life, and speakers shortened the name.
senses.whyCN: 计算机成了日常最常见的机器，说话者就把名称缩短了。

senses.title: A household or workshop appliance
senses.definition: a named device for one task, as in a washing or sewing machine
senses.definitionCN: 为单一任务命名的装置，如洗衣机或缝纫机
senses.example: The sewing machine has outlived three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 那台缝纫机已经比三位主人活得都久。
senses.why: a device is named by its task plus this general word, which is how the compound names spread.
senses.whyCN: 装置以「任务＋这个总称」命名，这类复合名称就是这样扩散的。

senses.title: A machine tool
senses.definition: a powered tool that cuts or shapes metal and other materials
senses.definitionCN: 切削或成型金属等材料的动力工具
senses.example: The new machine holds a tolerance of a hundredth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新机床能保持百分之一毫米的公差。
senses.why: in a workshop, the general word often means the tool that makes other parts.
senses.whyCN: 在车间里，这个总称常指制造其他零件的工具。

senses.title: To cut or shape by machine
senses.definition: to remove material or form a part with a powered tool
senses.definitionCN: 用动力工具去除材料或成型零件
senses.example: They machined the block in two passes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分两道工序加工了那块坯料。
senses.why: the noun became a verb the moment the tool's action needed a name.
senses.whyCN: 当工具的动作需要一个名称时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: A political organisation
senses.definition: the permanent staff and structure that win elections or hold power
senses.definitionCN: 赢得选举或维持权力的常设人员与结构
senses.example: The party machine decided the candidate before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 政党机器在投票之前就决定了候选人。
senses.why: an organisation that runs without sentiment is described by the most impersonal noun available.
senses.whyCN: 不带感情运转的组织，就用最非人格的名词来描述。

senses.title: An impersonal system of rule
senses.definition: the administrative apparatus of a state or large institution
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大型机构的行政装置
senses.example: The state machine ground down every small request.
senses.exampleCN: 国家机器把每一个小请求都磨掉了。
senses.why: the image of interlocking parts describes bureaucracy better than any abstract word.
senses.whyCN: 「咬合的部件」这一意象，比任何抽象词都更能描述官僚体系。

senses.title: A person who acts automatically
senses.definition: a person treated as incapable of independent thought
senses.definitionCN: 被视为无法独立思考的人
senses.example: They turned him into a machine that answered tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他变成一台只回答工单的机器。
senses.why: calling a person a machine denies judgement, which is the insult the word carries here.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作机器就是否认其判断力，这正是这个词在此处的贬义。

senses.title: Automated by computation
senses.definition: used before a noun for processes carried out by computers
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指由计算机完成的过程
senses.example: Machine translation improved, but it still misses tone.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译进步了，却仍抓不住语气。
senses.why: as a modifier, the word marks the shift from human to computed action.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标记从人工到计算动作的转移。

senses.title: The power unit of a vehicle
senses.definition: the engine and its housing in a boat, train or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 船、火车或车辆中的发动机及其外壳
senses.example: The fire machine kept its pump running for nine hours.
senses.exampleCN: 消防车的泵持续运转了九个小时。
senses.why: early industrial English called a powered vehicle a machine, and the usage survives in a few names.
senses.whyCN: 早期工业英语把动力车辆叫作 machine，这种用法在少数名称里留存下来。

intro.en: Machine came from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. It meant any contrivance long before it meant a powered device, and its computing and organisational senses are later extensions.
intro.cn: machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。它很久以前指任何巧妙装置，之后才指动力装置；计算机义与组织义是更晚的延伸。

items.en: Greek mekhane named a device, especially a stage crane or a siege engine, and also a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置，尤指舞台吊机或攻城器械，也指手段与办法。

items.en: Latin machina meant a structure, scaffold or engine, and the phrase deus ex machina came from the stage crane.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，短语 deus ex machina 就来自舞台吊机。

items.en: French machine entered English in the seventeenth century and covered any constructed device, not only powered ones.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪进入英语，指任何建造出来的装置，而不只是动力装置。

items.en: Steam and factory work narrowed machine toward devices with moving parts driven by power.
items.cn: 蒸汽与工厂作业把 machine 收窄为由动力驱动、带运动部件的装置。

items.en: The twentieth century added the computer and the party machine, both built on the image of parts working together.
items.cn: 二十世纪加上计算机与政党机器两义，二者都建立在「部件协同运转」的意象上。

items.en: Machining arose in workshops as the verb for what a machine tool does to metal.
items.cn: machining 在车间里产生，指机床对金属所做的加工。

note.en: The first group is the machine family in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for devices and systems.
note.cn: 第一组是 machine 词族的其他形态；第二组是装置与体系的相邻说法。

entries.definitionCN: 指机器的整体；一台机器可数，machinery 不可数。

entries.definition: A person who operates or makes machines; the noun names the equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作或制造机器的人；名词指设备。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; a machine is the thing repaired.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；machine 是被修的东西。

entries.definition: The set of parts that produces a motion; a machine contains one or more mechanisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的那组部件；一台机器包含一个或多个机构。

entries.definition: Any constructed thing made for a purpose, often small; a machine usually has moving parts and power.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的造的任何东西，常指小型；machine 通常有运动部件与动力。

entries.definition: A machine that converts energy into motion; it is a part of many machines.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量转成运动的机器；它是许多机器的一个部件。

entries.definition: An implement a person holds and guides; a machine supplies its own motion.
entries.definitionCN: 由人握持与引导的器具；machine 自己提供运动。

entries.definition: A set of equipment working as one, often for an experiment or an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体工作的一整套设备，常用于实验或机构。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊语来源与真实名词动词成对关系。

normal.en: Mekhane meant a stage crane, so a machine is first a thing that lifts and moves.
normal.cn: mekhane 原指舞台吊机，所以 machine 首先是能吊起与移动东西的装置。

normal.en: The verb forms are regular: machines, machined, machined, machining.
normal.cn: 动词形式规则：machines、machined、machined、machining。

normal.en: Task names build on it: washing machine, sewing machine, machine tool.
normal.cn: 任务名称在它之上构成：洗衣机、缝纫机、机床。

normal.en: The computing sense is simply the shortened name of the most common machine.
normal.cn: 计算机义不过是「最常用机器」的简称。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: machine a part, machine a surface.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：加工一个零件，加工一个表面。

abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的吊机放下一个神，而那神不过是一块画板。

examples.cn: 他们连夜加工了那只替换零件。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the general device to the computer, the appliance, the machine tool, the verb, the party machine, the state apparatus, the dehumanised person, computed processes and the vehicle's power unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从泛指的装置出发，经过计算机、家用器具、机床、动词用法、政党机器、国家机器、被机械化的人、计算化流程，最后到车辆动力机组。

branches.en: DEVICES: any working assembly, and the named appliance built on that pattern.
branches.cn: 装置：任何做功的组合体，以及按此模式命名的器具。

branches.en: COMPUTATION: the computer itself, and processes carried out by computed action.
branches.cn: 计算：计算机本身，以及由计算动作完成的过程。

branches.en: TOOL AND ACTION: the machine tool, and the verb for what it does to metal.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：机床，以及它对金属所做加工的动词。

branches.en: ORGANISED POWER: the party machine, and the administrative apparatus of a state.
branches.cn: 组织化的权力：政党机器，以及国家的行政装置。

branches.en: THE MECHANICAL FIGURE: a person reduced to a machine, and a vehicle's engine unit.
branches.cn: 机械化的形象：被降为机器的人，以及车辆的动力机组。

intro.en: Machine is a borrowed noun with no living affix; its family adds -ery, -ist, -ing and compound forms.

definition_en: suffering from a serious mental illness, extremely angry in everyday speech, wildly enthusiastic, or foolish beyond reason

scene: 夜里的急诊走廊上，一位老人对着空气大声争辩，护士轻声请来值班医生。The old man had gone mad and kept arguing with people who were not there.
sceneCN: 这里 mad 是「精神失常的、发疯的」（第 1 个义项：神志不清）；句意为老人已经疯了，一直跟并不存在的人争论。图中可辨识物件：急诊走廊的灯、护士站、病历夹。

pos.zh: 发疯的；精神失常的；生气的；狂热的；愚蠢的

collocations.zh: 彻底疯了；疯得不可理喻

derivatives.zh: 由 mad 加 -ness 构成，义为「疯狂；精神失常」
由 mad 加 -ly 构成，义为「疯狂地；非正式口语中作『极其』」
由 mad 与 man 复合，义为「疯子；失去理智的男人」

senses.title: Mentally ill and out of touch with reality
senses.definition: suffering from a serious mental illness, so that the person cannot think or behave as others do
senses.definitionCN: 患有严重精神疾病，思考和举止与常人不同
senses.example: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。
senses.why: Old English gemǣd described a mind that had been altered out of its proper state, so illness of the mind is the oldest recorded sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemǣd 描述的是神志被改变、脱离正常状态，所以「心智患病」是这个词最早的记录义项。

senses.title: Very angry
senses.definition: extremely annoyed about something, in everyday informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中因某事而极为恼火
senses.example: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。
senses.why: Anger was pictured as a passing disturbance of the mind, and the word for a disordered mind slid into the word for a hot temper.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被想象成心智一时的失序，于是那个表示「头脑不正常」的词便滑向了「火气上来」这层意思。

senses.title: Wildly enthusiastic
senses.definition: so enthusiastic about someone or something that ordinary caution disappears
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物极为热衷，连平常的谨慎都没有了
senses.example: He is mad about vintage motorcycles and spends every weekend in the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他痴迷老式摩托车，每个周末都泡在车库里。
senses.why: Enthusiasm that sweeps away caution looks like the same loss of control, so the word moved from illness and anger to passion.
senses.whyCN: 那种把谨慎一扫而空的热情，看上去是同一种失控，于是这个词从疾病、愤怒又走到了迷恋。

senses.title: Foolish and ill judged
senses.definition: wildly foolish, used of plans or actions that no sensible person would attempt
senses.definitionCN: 极其愚蠢的，用于形容任何明白人都不会尝试的计划或举动
senses.example: Crossing the river in that storm was a mad thing to do.
senses.exampleCN: 在那样一场暴风雨里过河，是件极其愚蠢的事。
senses.why: Before it named illness, the word already meant foolish, so poor judgement remains the quiet base under every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 在指疾病之前，这个词早已表示「愚蠢」，所以「判断力差」一直是后来各义项底下沉默的底色。

intro.en: Mad is an Old English word for a disordered mind; its later senses of anger and passion grew from that base, and its deeper root is debated.
intro.cn: mad 是古英语中表示「神志失常」的词；后来「愤怒」与「痴迷」的意思都从这个底子长出来，更早的语源仍有争论。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic adjective, usually taken to mean changed or altered, and often explained as a mind shifted out of its normal state; the exact formation is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个重构的日耳曼语形容词，一般认为意为「被改变的」，常被解释为神志偏出了正常状态；确切构成仍不确定。

items.en: Gemǣd is recorded in Old English for foolish and insane, and the ge- prefix gathers the word into a completed state.
items.cn: gemǣd 在古英语中记录为愚蠢的、精神失常的，前缀 ge- 把词收进一种已完成的状态。

items.en: Middle English drops the prefix and keeps mad, and by the fourteenth century the word also means angrily excited.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉前缀，保留 mad；到十四世纪，这个词也指「怒气冲冲的」。

items.en: The phrases mad about and mad for come to mean passionately fond, first of people and then of pursuits.
items.cn: 短语 mad about 与 mad for 开始表示「极其喜爱」，先用于人，后用于嗜好。

items.en: Modern English keeps the medical sense, uses mad for anger chiefly in informal American speech, and builds compounds such as mad cow and mad rush.
items.cn: 现代英语保留医学义项，「生气」义主要用于非正式美式口语，并造出疯牛病、疯狂冲刺一类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives, a compound and one word that merely shares the spelling; the near group gathers words for a disturbed mind and for anger.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词、一个复合词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示心智失常与愤怒的词。

entries.definition: The state of being insane, or wildly foolish behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常的状态；疯狂的行为；由 mad 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: In a wild or frantic way, and informally very much.
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂地；非正式口语中作「极其」；由 mad 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A man who is insane or acts with reckless violence.
entries.definitionCN: 疯子；行为狂暴失去理智的男人；由 mad 与 man 复合。

entries.definition: A polite form of address to a woman; only the spelling is close, the origin is French and unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 对女性的礼貌称呼；与 mad 只是拼写相近，词源来自法语，二者无关。

entries.definition: Wildly unreasonable or insane, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指极不理智或精神失常的。

entries.definition: Seriously mentally ill, or utterly foolish.
entries.definitionCN: 患严重精神病的；也指极其荒唐的。

entries.definition: Extremely angry.
entries.definitionCN: 极其愤怒的。

entries.definition: Feeling strong displeasure about something.
entries.definitionCN: 因某事而感到强烈不快的。

normalIntro.en: The word is an Old English name for a mind out of order, and its family keeps returning to illness, temper and the passions that overrule caution.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语给「失序的心智」起的名字，它的同族词反复回到疾病、脾气，以及压过谨慎的激情。

normal.en: Old English already had gemǣd for foolish and insane, and modern mad is that word with its prefix worn away.
normal.cn: 古英语已有 gemǣd 表示愚蠢与精神失常，现代 mad 就是磨掉了前缀的那个词。

normal.en: The Old English prefix ge- often marks a completed state, so gemǣd pictured a mind that had been changed into something else.
normal.cn: 古英语前缀 ge- 常标记一种已完成的状态，所以 gemǣd 画出的是被改换成了别样东西的心智。

normal.en: Three ordinary endings carry the family: -ness makes madness, -ly makes madly, and man makes madman.
normal.cn: 三个常规词尾撑起这个词族：-ness 造出 madness，-ly 造出 madly，man 与 mad 合成 madman。

normal.en: Mad for anger is normal in American speech, while British speakers generally say angry instead.
normal.cn: 用 mad 表示生气在美式口语里很自然，英国人一般还是说 angry。

normal.en: To be mad about a hobby means far more than liking it: the hobby has taken over the weekends.
normal.cn: 对一项嗜好 mad about，远不只是「喜欢」：那项嗜好已经占满了周末。

abstract.en: A mind knocked out of place, like a clock whose hands have been bent by a blow.
abstract.cn: 一颗被撞离原位的心，就像一只被一击打歪了指针的钟。

abstract.en: Illness, anger and passion share one word because all three are states that take over the will.
abstract.cn: 疾病、愤怒与激情共用一个词，因为这三者都是接管了意志的状态。

abstract.en: Mad is what English says when reason has let go of the steering wheel.
abstract.cn: 当理智松开方向盘时，英语就说 mad。

examples.en: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
examples.cn: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。

examples.en: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
examples.cn: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。

examples.en: Many drivers go mad in the city's evening traffic.
examples.cn: 许多司机在城市的晚高峰里被逼得发疯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦德」——麦德脾气火爆，一点小事就跳起来发疯；记住 mad 是发疯、生气。

root: 古英语 gemǣd（愚蠢的、精神失常的），一般认为来自原始日耳曼语一个意为「被改变的」重构形式，确切构成存疑；中古英语磨去前缀 ge-，写作 mad。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mind out of its proper state; the senses then divide into mental illness, passing anger, burning enthusiasm and plain foolishness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是偏离正常状态的心智；义项由此分成精神疾病、一时的怒气、炽热的迷恋，以及单纯的愚蠢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man arguing earnestly with an empty chair, seeing a world no one else can see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人对着空椅子认真争辩，看见别人看不见的世界。

branches.en: a doctor watching a patient argue with an empty chair
branches.cn: 医生看着病人对空椅子争论

branches.en: a slammed door and a voice rising in the hall
branches.cn: 门被摔上，走廊里的嗓门高起来

branches.en: a man who cannot stop talking about his new motorbike
branches.cn: 一个人停不下来说他的新车

branches.en: a garage floor covered in half-repaired engines
branches.cn: 车库里满地是修了一半的发动机

branches.en: a boat pushed out into a black storm
branches.cn: 一条小船被推进漆黑的暴风雨

intro.en: An Old English adjective for a disordered mind, a Germanic prefix that has since worn away, and three English endings carry the word from illness to temper and passion.
intro.cn: 一个表示心智失序的古英语形容词、一个后来磨掉不存的日耳曼前缀，再加三个英语词尾，把这个词从疾病带到脾气与激情。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin insanus means insane, but it is built on a different root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 insanus 意为「精神失常的」，但它建立在另一个词根上。

definition_zh: 夫人；女士；太太；小姐；对女性的尊称；（俚语）鸨母
definition_en: a polite and respectful way of addressing a woman, or a woman who manages a brothel
core_image: 一位被恭恭敬敬称呼的女士：礼貌的称呼指向一位体面女性
scene: 酒店的经理亲自上前招呼那位提着行李的客人。May I help you with your luggage, madam?
sceneCN: 这里 madam 是「女士、夫人」（第 1 个义项：对女性的礼貌尊称）；句意为经理恭敬地询问这位女客人是否需要帮忙提行李。图中可辨识物件：酒店大堂、行李箱、前台。

pos.zh: 名词：夫人、女士、太太、小姐；对女性的尊称；（俚语）鸨母

collocations.zh: 主席女士（对女主席的称呼）
先生或女士（不识对方时的称呼）

derivatives.zh: madam 的口语缩略形式，义为「夫人、女士」，多用于英式英语和服务场合
法语借词，义为「夫人、太太」，用于称呼说法语的已婚女性或称呼法语女教师
由同一拉丁词根经古法语进入英语，义为「女士；（英国）女爵士」

senses.title: A polite way to address a woman
senses.definition: a polite and respectful word used when speaking to a woman whose name you do not know
senses.definitionCN: 在不认识对方姓名时礼貌恭敬地称呼女性的用语
senses.example: May I take your coat, madam?
senses.exampleCN: 夫人，要我为您拿外套吗？
senses.why: The phrase originally meant my lady, so calling a woman madam places her in the honoured position of a lady.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本的字面意思是「我的夫人」，所以称呼一位女性 madam，等于把她放到受尊敬的「贵妇」位置上。

senses.title: A formal address to a customer
senses.titleCN: 对女性顾客的正式称呼
senses.definition: a formal word used by shop assistants, waiters or hotel staff to address a female customer
senses.definitionCN: 店员、侍者或酒店工作人员称呼女性顾客的正式用语
senses.example: The waiter handed her the menu and said, "Madam, the soup of the day is mushroom."
senses.exampleCN: 侍者递上菜单说：「女士，今日例汤是蘑菇汤。」
senses.why: Service speech keeps the old courtly habit: the customer is treated as a lady of rank, so the honourable title survives.
senses.whyCN: 服务用语保留了旧日的宫廷礼节：顾客被当作有身份的贵妇来对待，因此这个尊称一直流传下来。

senses.title: A title in formal letters
senses.definition: a word used in the opening of a formal letter to a woman, as in Dear Madam
senses.definitionCN: 用于写给女性的正式信函开头，如 Dear Madam
senses.example: The letter began "Dear Sir or Madam" because the writer did not know who would read it.
senses.exampleCN: 信的开头是「尊敬的先生或女士」，因为写信人不知道谁会读到它。
senses.why: When the reader's name and sex are unknown, the polite title stands in for the name itself.
senses.whyCN: 当收信人的姓名和性别都不明确时，这个礼貌称呼就代替姓名来充当称呼。

senses.title: A woman of authority
senses.definition: a word used before an official title to address a woman holding that position, as in Madam Chairman or Madam President
senses.definitionCN: 用于官职前称呼担任该职位的女性，如 Madam Chairman、Madam President
senses.example: Madam Chairman, may I present the quarterly report to the board?
senses.exampleCN: 主席女士，我可以向董事会提交季度报告吗？
senses.why: A title of respect can be attached to any position of power, so the word marks the office, not just the person.
senses.whyCN: 尊称可以加在任何有权力的职位之前，因此这个词标记的是职位，而不只是某个人。

senses.title: A haughty or self-important woman
senses.definition: a humorous or critical word for a woman who behaves as if she deserves great respect and special treatment
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑或批评用语，指举止傲慢、自认为该受特殊待遇的女性
senses.example: She swept into the office like a little madam who owned the whole building.
senses.exampleCN: 她大摇大摆走进办公室，活像个把整栋楼都当成自己家的小姐。
senses.why: The honourable title can be used ironically: giving noble treatment to someone who merely acts noble is a common form of mockery.
senses.whyCN: 尊称可以被反用：对只是装出高贵样子的人刻意使用敬称，正是一种常见的讽刺手法。

senses.title: A brothel manager
senses.definition: in slang, the female manager of a brothel, often capitalized as Madam
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指妓院的女经营者，常以大写 Madam 出现
senses.example: In the novel, the madam controlled every room in the house and every coin in the till.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里，这位鸨母掌管着屋里的每个房间和钱柜里的每一枚硬币。
senses.why: The manager runs the house the way a lady runs a great household, so the title of household authority was transferred to her trade.
senses.whyCN: 经营者像贵妇掌管大宅门一样掌管那栋房子，于是「家宅掌权者」的头衔被转移到了这个行当上。

intro.en: Madam is a shortened form of a French phrase meaning my lady, and its root is the Latin word for the mistress of a house.
intro.cn: madam 是法语短语「我的夫人」的缩略形式，其词根是拉丁语中「女主人」一词。

items.en: Latin domina meant mistress, lady of the house, the feminine of dominus lord. It later gave Dame and dame in many European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语 domina 意为「女主人、夫人」，是 dominus「主人」的阴性形式；它后来在多种欧洲语言中产生 dame 一词。

items.en: Old French combined the possessive ma with dame into ma dame, a respectful way of addressing a lady of rank.
items.cn: 古法语把物主词 ma 与 dame 合成 ma dame，即「我的夫人」，是对有身份女性的敬称。

items.en: In speech the two words fused into a single form madame, which travelled to England with the French-speaking court.
items.cn: 在口语中两个词融合为单一名词 madame，并随讲法语的宫廷传入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English borrowed madame in the thirteenth century and soon clipped it to madam, and further to ma'am in casual speech.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪借入 madame，很快截短为 madam，口语中又进一步缩略为 ma'am。

items.en: The polite senses stayed central, while the ironic use for a haughty woman and the slang use for a brothel manager grew out of the same title of authority.
items.cn: 礼貌义项始终是核心，而讽刺傲慢女性和俚语指鸨母的用法，都是从同一个「掌权者尊称」里长出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the whole my-lady family in several languages; the near-meaning group gathers other polite ways of addressing a woman.
note.cn: 形近组收「我的夫人」这一词族在多种语言中的形式；近义组收其他称呼女性的礼貌用语。

entries.definition: The French word for a married woman, used in English for French-speaking married women or French teachers.
entries.definitionCN: 法语中对已婚女性的称呼，英语里用于称呼说法语的已婚女性或法语女教师。

entries.definition: The French title for an unmarried woman, literally my little lady.
entries.definitionCN: 法语中对未婚女性的称呼，字面意思是「我的小夫人」。

entries.definition: A woman of rank or, in Britain, a woman awarded an honour equivalent to a knighthood.
entries.definitionCN: 有身份的女性；在英国指获授相当于骑士勋位的女性爵士。

entries.definition: The rank or title of a dame, formed from dame plus the suffix -hood.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dame 加后缀 -hood 构成，义为「女爵士的地位或头衔」。

entries.definition: A masked costume or a game tile; it merely resembles the Latin root in spelling and belongs to another word history.
entries.definitionCN: 指化妆舞会的假面斗篷或多米诺骨牌；只是拼写与拉丁词根相近，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: The clipped spoken form of madam, common in British and Southern American speech and in service situations.
entries.definitionCN: madam 的口语缩略形式，常见于英式英语、美国南方和服务场合。

entries.definition: The Italian my lady, used for the Virgin Mary and in polite Italian address.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语「我的夫人」，用于指圣母马利亚，也是意大利语的敬称。

entries.definition: A general polite word for a woman, describing manners or rank rather than serving as a direct address.
entries.definitionCN: 对女性的一般礼貌用词，描述教养或身份，通常不作面对面称呼。

entries.definition: A woman in a position of authority over a household, from the same Latin root dominus.
entries.definitionCN: 掌管家务、拥有权威的女性，来自同一拉丁词根 dominus。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase and the word's most common polite settings.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语短语和这个词最常见的礼貌场合。

normal.en: Madam is ma dame, my lady: two French words glued into one.
normal.cn: madam 就是 ma dame（我的夫人）：两个法语词粘成了一个词。

normal.en: The root dame comes from Latin domina, the mistress of a house.
normal.cn: 词根 dame 来自拉丁语 domina，即一家之女主人。

normal.en: Letters that do not know the reader open with Dear Sir or Madam.
normal.cn: 不知道收信人的信件抬头写 Dear Sir or Madam。

normal.en: Shop staff and hotel clerks keep the word alive when serving women.
normal.cn: 店员和酒店职员接待女客时至今仍用这个词。

normal.en: In speech it shrinks to ma'am, one swallowed syllable.
normal.cn: 口语中它缩略成 ma'am，只剩一个吞掉的音节。

abstract.en: Picture a curtsy in a palace corridor: the word is that bow, folded small enough to carry in your mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象宫廷走廊里的一次屈膝礼：这个词就是那个礼，被折叠得刚好能放进嘴里。

abstract.en: Ma and dame sit side by side; whenever you own something politely in French, you put ma in front of it.
abstract.cn: ma 和 dame 并肩而立：法语里礼貌地「拥有」什么，就把 ma 放在前面。

abstract.en: One title, many women: the honoured lady, the haughty little madam, the woman who runs the house behind the door.
abstract.cn: 同一个称呼对应不同的女性：受尊敬的夫人、傲慢的大小姐、门后掌管全家事务的女主人。

examples.en: Madam, your table is ready; please follow me.
examples.cn: 女士，您的餐桌已备好，请跟我来。

core_image: 一顶高礼帽、一根细棒，白鸽从空空的袖口里扑棱飞出来
scene: 后台的道具箱里放着假鸽子、彩带和一顶高礼帽，幕布只拉开一半。The audience applauded as the magic began in a puff of smoke.
sceneCN: 这里 magic 是「魔术、戏法」（第 2 个义项：舞台上的障眼技艺）；句意为观众在一阵烟雾中迎来魔术开场，随即鼓起掌来。图中可辨识物件：高礼帽、彩带、半开的幕布。

senses.title: Supernatural power used to change events
senses.definition: the supposed power to make things happen by charms, spells or secret forces beyond nature
senses.definitionCN: 通过咒语、符咒或超自然隐秘力量左右事物的、被认为存在的能力
senses.example: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。
senses.why: Greek magos named a Persian priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became the ordinary word for power over events that nature does not explain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 magos 指波斯的占星祭司，这类祭司的技艺后来成了「支配自然无法解释之事的力量」的日常说法。

senses.title: Conjuring tricks performed on stage
senses.definition: the art of producing baffling effects by sleight of hand, hidden props and misdirection
senses.definitionCN: 依靠手上功夫、暗藏道具与转移注意，制造出令人困惑效果的行当
senses.example: Her act mixed quick card magic with a dove that vanished from a hat.
senses.exampleCN: 她的节目把快速的纸牌魔术和一只从帽子里消失的鸽子混在一起。
senses.why: A stage performer copies the effects the old craft claimed, so the same noun now names a trick that everyone knows is a trick.
senses.whyCN: 舞台艺人复制了古老技艺号称能做到的效果，于是同一个名词如今指一场人人都知道是假的戏法。

senses.title: A compelling, unexplained charm
senses.definition: a quality in a place, person or moment that seems to work on people beyond ordinary cause
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某人或某一刻身上那种仿佛超出常理、能打动人的特质
senses.example: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。
senses.why: If magic means power that acts without visible cause, then a place that moves people without explanation can simply be said to have magic in it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 magic 指没有可见原因就起作用的力量，那么一个说不清为何打动人的地方，自然就可以说身上带着魔力。

senses.title: Wonderful and enchanting, as an adjective
senses.definition: used beside a noun for something that seems to work beyond ordinary means or feels enchanting
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词旁边，形容某物仿佛以超乎常理的方式奏效，或令人觉得着迷
senses.example: The garden looked magic under the first snow of winter.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下时，那座园子看起来像被施了魔法。
senses.why: Once the noun names a power that changes things, placing it beside another noun turns it into a plain adjective for the effect.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词指一种改变事物的力量，把它放到另一个名词旁边，就自然变成了描述那种效果的形容词。

intro.en: Magic is a word borrowed from the title of a foreign priesthood; it then split into a claimed supernatural art, a harmless stage act, a felt charm and a plain adjective.
intro.cn: magic 是从一个外来祭司称号借来的词；它后来分成号称的超自然技艺、人畜无害的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及一个普通形容词。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old Persian maguš, a member of a priestly class who read the stars and performed rites.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追到古波斯语 maguš，指主持仪式、观测星象的祭司阶层成员。

items.en: Greek adopted the title as magos for a Persian priest or a wandering wise man, and the abstract craft was called magikē.
items.cn: 希腊语把这个称号借作 magos，指波斯祭司或游走的智者，而那种抽象的技艺被称为 magikē。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as magicus, and the related noun named the art itself rather than the man.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 magicus，相关的名词则指那门技艺本身，而不是那个人。

items.en: Old French magique carried noun and adjective into medieval Europe, and English borrowed the forms in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 magique 把名词与形容词一起带进中世纪的欧洲，英语在十三、十四世纪借入这些形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps magic for the occult art and for the stage act, adds the figurative charm, and uses the bare noun before other nouns as an adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 magic 指神秘技艺与舞台表演，加上比喻性的魅力，并把光秃秃的名词放在其他名词前当形容词用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and the biblical plural of the priestly title; the near group gathers other words for magic arts and for tricks of the senses.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词与那个祭司称号的圣经复数；近义组收其他表示法术以及感官幻象的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the title of a foreign priest, and its family keeps returning to hidden knowledge, stage deception and the charm that needs no explanation.

normal.cn: 拉丁语 magicus 与古法语 magique 把词带到英语，英语把词尾缩短成 magic。

normal.en: Magician adds -ian to name the person, magical adds -al for the quality, and magically adds -ly for the manner.
normal.cn: magician 加 -ian 指人，magical 加 -al 指性质，magically 再加 -ly 指方式。

normal.en: A magic wand and a magic trick keep the stage sense, while black magic keeps the darker ritual sense.

abstract.en: Magic survives because people still want a short name for effects they cannot explain.

abstract.en: The same word covers a trick you can learn and a power you can only imagine.

root: 希腊语 magos（波斯的祭司、占星师）→ 希腊语 magikē（祭司的技艺）→ 拉丁语 magicus → 古法语 magique → 英语 magic；一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a power that acts without visible cause; the senses then divide into the claimed occult art, the stage trick that copies it, a felt charm and an everyday adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种没有可见原因就起作用的力量；义项由此分成号称的神秘技艺、复制它的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及日常形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall hat, a thin wand, and a white dove bursting out of an empty sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶高礼帽、一根细棒，白鸽从空空的袖口里扑棱飞出。

branches.cn: 老广场上方灯笼次第亮起

branches.en: snow settling on a silent garden
branches.cn: 雪落在寂静的园子里

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms magicus and magus are recorded, and both descend from Greek magos, which in turn is generally traced to Old Persian maguš.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 magicus 与 magus 均有记录，二者都出自希腊语 magos，而后者一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

definition_zh: 邮件；信件；邮政系统；电子邮件；锁子甲；邮寄
definition_en: letters and parcels sent by post; the postal system; electronic messages; armour of linked metal rings; to send something by post
core_image: 门垫上堆着一叠信封，邮戳还带着油墨味
scene: 雨下了一整夜，门廊的脚垫上积着水，伞桶旁边多了一只湿透的牛皮纸袋。The mail had been pushed through the slot and now lay in a damp heap on the floor.
sceneCN: 这里指寄来的信件与包裹（第 1 个义项：邮件）；句意为邮件从投信口塞进来，湿漉漉地堆在地板上。

pos.zh: 邮件；信件；邮政系统；电子邮件；锁子甲
邮寄；发送

derivatives.zh: 由 mail 加 -er 构成，义为「邮寄者；邮递包装」
由 mail 加 -ing 构成，义为「邮寄；寄出的邮件」
由 electronic 的首字母 e 与 mail 复合，义为「电子邮件；发电子邮件」
由 mail 与 box 复合，义为「邮箱；信箱」

senses.title: Letters and parcels sent by post
senses.definition: letters, cards and parcels delivered through the postal system
senses.definitionCN: 通过邮政系统投递的信件、卡片和包裹
senses.example: The mail arrives before noon on weekdays.
senses.exampleCN: 工作日里邮件在中午前送到。
senses.why: The word first named the travelling bag that carried letters, and the contents of the bag took the name of the bag.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指装信件的旅行袋，后来袋中之物沿用了袋子的名字。

senses.title: The postal system
senses.definition: the public service that collects and delivers letters and parcels
senses.definitionCN: 负责收寄和投递信件、包裹的公共服务
senses.example: The island has no daily mail service in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛在冬天没有每日邮政服务。
senses.why: Once the bag and its contents were called mail, the network that moved them took the same name, because the service existed to handle the mail.
senses.whyCN: 袋子及其内容物都叫 mail 之后，负责运送它们的网络也用了同一个名字，因为这项服务的存在就是为了处理邮件。

senses.title: Electronic messages
senses.definition: messages sent and received through the internet, especially in an email account
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网收发、存放在电子邮件账户里的信息
senses.example: Her mail was full of unread messages after the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期过后，她的邮箱里全是未读信息。
senses.why: Electronic messages borrowed the name because they arrive in an inbox, just as paper letters arrive through a letterbox.
senses.whyCN: 电子消息借用这个名字，因为它们进入收件箱，就像纸质信件从信箱口进来一样。

senses.title: Armour of interlinked metal rings
senses.definition: flexible armour made of small metal rings linked into a mesh
senses.definitionCN: 由小金属环连接成网、可以随身体弯曲的铠甲
senses.example: The knight's mail protected him from a glancing sword blow.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士的锁子甲挡下了一记擦过的剑击。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word: Old French maille meant a mesh, from Latin macula, and linked rings form exactly such a mesh.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词：古法语 maille 意为网眼，源自拉丁语 macula，而环环相扣的金属正构成这样的网。

senses.title: To send something by post
senses.definition: to put a letter or parcel into the postal system for delivery
senses.definitionCN: 把信件或包裹交给邮政系统投递
senses.example: Please mail the signed form before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五之前把签好的表格寄出去。
senses.why: The verb is simply the noun put to work: to mail something is to hand it over to the mail.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词直接转用：mail 某物，就是把它交给邮政系统。

intro.en: Mail is two words under one spelling: a bag word that became letters and postal service, and a mesh word that became armour.
intro.cn: mail 是同一拼写下的两个词：一个「袋子」词变成信件与邮政，一个「网眼」词变成铠甲。

items.en: The postal sense starts from Old French male, a bag or wallet carried on a journey.
items.cn: 邮政义从古法语 male 开始，那是旅途中携带的袋子或钱袋。

items.en: The bag word is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish form such as *malha, though the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个「袋子」词一般追溯到重构的法兰克语形式（如 *malha），但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: The armour sense comes from a different Old French word, maille, meaning a mesh or ring.
items.cn: 铠甲义来自另一个古法语词 maille，意为网眼或环。

items.en: Latin macula meant a spot or a mesh in a net, and it is the recorded source of maille.
items.cn: 拉丁语 macula 意为斑点或网中的网眼，是 maille 有记载的来源。

items.en: Modern English keeps both histories under one spelling and adds email, a new sense built on the postal one.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条历史并排在同一种拼写下，并新增了建立在邮政义上的 email。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives of the postal word; the near-meaning group gathers words for letters and for sending them.
note.cn: 形近组收邮政义词的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示信件与寄送的词。

entries.definition: Electronic mail; also the verb for sending it.
entries.definitionCN: 电子邮件；也指发送电子邮件的动作。

entries.definition: A box or address where mail is received.
entries.definitionCN: 接收邮件的箱子或地址。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to deliver mail.
entries.definitionCN: 以投递邮件为职业的人。

entries.definition: A bag used to carry letters and parcels.
entries.definitionCN: 用来装信件和包裹的袋子。

entries.definition: The public system for sending letters, or to send a letter.
entries.definitionCN: 寄信的公共系统，或指寄信。

entries.definition: A written message sent to someone, usually on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 写给某人的书面信息，通常写在纸上。

entries.definition: An object or set of objects wrapped for sending.
entries.definitionCN: 包装好准备寄送的物品。

entries.definition: Letters exchanged between people.
entries.definitionCN: 人们之间往来的书信。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a bag, a bundle of letters, a postal network, an inbox and a coat of rings, all under one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时装着袋子、信件、邮政网络、收件箱和一件环甲，全部共用一种拼写。

normal.en: Mail first meant a travelling bag, so the word began with a container rather than with paper.
normal.cn: mail 最初指旅行袋，所以这个词的起点是容器，而不是纸张。

normal.en: The postal sense and the armour sense look identical but have separate histories, one from a bag and one from a mesh.
normal.cn: 邮政义和铠甲义拼写相同，却各有来历：一个出自袋子，一个出自网眼。

normal.en: Old French maille and Latin macula connect the armour to a net of rings, which is why chain mail is described as a mesh.
normal.cn: 古法语 maille 与拉丁语 macula 把铠甲连到环网，所以锁子甲被形容为网。

normal.en: Email simply puts the prefix e- for electronic in front of mail, keeping the old idea of messages waiting for you.
normal.cn: email 只是把表示电子的前缀 e- 放在 mail 前面，保留了「消息在等你」的旧意象。

normal.en: Mail carrier and mail order show the word naming both the thing delivered and the system that delivers it.
normal.cn: mail carrier 与 mail order 表明这个词既指被投递的东西，也指投递它的系统。

abstract.en: A wet bundle of envelopes on a doormat makes the abstract postal system visible for a moment.
abstract.cn: 门垫上湿漉漉的一叠信封，让抽象的邮政系统在一瞬间变得可见。

abstract.en: A bag becomes letters, letters become a service, and the service becomes an inbox: one name travels the whole route.
abstract.cn: 袋子变成信件，信件变成服务，服务又变成收件箱：一个名字走完了整条路线。

abstract.en: Chain mail and posted mail share only a spelling; remembering that they are strangers keeps both meanings clear.
abstract.cn: 锁子甲与邮寄的邮件只共享拼写；记住它们是陌生人，两个意思才不会混。

examples.en: The mail arrives before noon on weekdays.
examples.cn: 工作日里邮件在中午前送到。

examples.en: Please mail the signed form before Friday.
examples.cn: 请在周五之前把签好的表格寄出去。

examples.en: The knight's mail protected him from a glancing sword blow.
examples.cn: 骑士的锁子甲挡下了一记擦过的剑击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妹儿」——把信交给小妹儿去寄；记住 mail 是邮件、邮寄。

root: 邮政义一般认为来自古法语 male（旅行袋）；铠甲义来自古法语 maille（网眼），后者可追溯到拉丁语 macula。两条来源在英语里拼成同一个词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is letters in transit; the postal service, the electronic inbox and the verb all grow from it, while the armour sense follows a separate Latin line.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是运送中的信件；邮政系统、电子收件箱与动词都由此长出，而铠甲义则走另一条拉丁线索。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of envelopes on a doormat and an old cloth bag that once carried them.
core.cn: 核心意象：门垫上的一叠信封，以及一只曾经装过这些信件的旧布袋。

branches.en: a damp stack of envelopes on a doormat
branches.cn: 门垫上湿漉漉的一叠信封

branches.en: a post office truck moving through a winter village
branches.cn: 邮车穿过冬日村庄

branches.en: an inbox glowing with unread messages
branches.cn: 收件箱里亮着未读消息

branches.en: a knight's sleeve of linked rings catching the light
branches.cn: 骑士衣袖上的连环映着光

branches.en: a hand dropping a signed form into a letterbox
branches.cn: 一只手把签好的表格投进信箱

intro.cn: 这个词由古法语的「袋子」名词、拉丁语的「网眼」名词，以及延伸两条线索的英语复合词共同支撑。

definition_zh: 主要的；最重要的；主管道；总线路；市电；大海
definition_en: most important or largest; a principal pipe or cable for water, gas or electricity; the public power supply; the open sea
core_image: 一张地图上，最粗的那条路通向城市中心
scene: 暴雪过后的清晨，维修车沿着城外最宽的那条公路往城里开。The main road into the valley was still blocked by snow.
sceneCN: 这里指最重要、最主要的那条（第 1 个义项：主要的）；句意为通往山谷的主路仍被雪堵住。

pos.zh: 主要的；最重要的
主管道；总线路；市电；大海

derivatives.zh: 由 main 加 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；大部分地」
由 main 与 land 复合，义为「大陆；本土」
由 main 与 stream 复合，义为「主流」
由 main 与 stay 复合，义为「支柱；主要依靠」

senses.title: Most important or largest
senses.definition: being the most important, largest or most influential of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中最重要、最大或最有影响力的
senses.example: The main reason for the delay was the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的主要原因是天气。
senses.why: Old English mægen meant strength, so what is main is what carries the greatest weight in a situation.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mægen 意为力量，因此 main 指在某个局面里分量最重的那一个。

senses.title: A principal pipe or cable
senses.definition: the largest pipe or cable that carries water, gas or electricity to many places
senses.definitionCN: 把水、燃气或电输送到许多地方的最大管道或线路
senses.example: A burst water main flooded the lower street.
senses.exampleCN: 一根爆裂的自来水主管淹没了地势较低的那条街。
senses.why: The adjective naming the chief thing became a noun for the chief channel, because that pipe carries the greatest volume and serves the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 形容「主要之物」的形容词转成名词，指最主要的输送通道，因为那根管道输送量最大、服务整个网络。

senses.title: The open sea
senses.definition: the open ocean, especially when seen as a great expanse away from land
senses.definitionCN: 开阔的海洋，尤指远离陆地、显得辽阔无边的海面
senses.example: The ship sailed out into the main at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船在黎明时驶向外海。
senses.why: The old sense of main as great or mighty survived at sea, where the open ocean is the great expanse beyond the shore.
senses.whyCN: main 古义「宏大、强大」在海上留存下来：岸边之外那一片开阔水域就是宏大的存在。

senses.title: The public electricity supply
senses.definition: the ordinary electricity supply provided to homes and buildings, especially in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 供给住宅和建筑的常规电力，尤见于英式用法
senses.example: The lamp can run on batteries or on the mains.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯可以用电池，也可以接市电。
senses.why: British speakers call the shared public supply the mains because it is the central source every building draws from, like the main pipe of a water system.
senses.whyCN: 英式说法把公共供电称作 the mains，因为它是每栋建筑都从中取电的中心来源，就像供水系统里的主管道。

intro.en: Main comes from a Germanic noun for strength; the adjective for the strongest or chief thing later became a noun for the chief channel.
intro.cn: main 来自日耳曼语中表示力量的名词；表示最强、首要之物的形容词后来转成指主要通道的名词。

items.en: The adjective comes from mægen, a noun meaning power, strength or force.
items.cn: 这个形容词来自 mægen，一个意为力量、力气、威力的名词。

items.en: The reconstructed base *maginam carried the same idea of strength and ability, and it also lies behind might and may.
items.cn: 重构词根 *maginam 同样表示力量与能力，might 与 may 也出自这里。

items.en: Middle English main kept the sense of chief or principal, and the word began to describe the leading road, pipe or clause.
items.cn: 中古英语 main 保留「首要、主要」的意思，并开始用来描述最主要的道路、管道或从句。

items.en: The noun main narrowed to the principal channel of a water or gas system, while the sea sense remained poetic.
items.cn: 名词 main 缩小为供水或燃气系统的主管道，而「大海」义仍带诗意。

items.en: Modern British usage adds the mains for public electricity, and 「main road」, 「main idea」 and 「main clause」 fix the adjective in daily speech.
items.cn: 现代英式用法又用 the mains 指公共供电，「main road」「main idea」「main clause」则把形容词固定在日常表达里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on main or on its Germanic root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what ranks first.
note.cn: 形近组收由 main 或其日耳曼词根构成的词；近义组收表示排在最前的形容词。

entries.definition: Chiefly, or for the most part.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；大部分地。

entries.definition: The principal land mass, as opposed to islands.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于岛屿而言的主要陆地；大陆。

entries.definition: The ideas or practices accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被多数人接受的思想或做法；主流。

entries.definition: The person or thing that provides the chief support.
entries.definitionCN: 提供主要支撑的人或事物；支柱。

entries.definition: Most important; the leader of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的；团体负责人。

entries.definition: First in importance; the head of a school.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的；学校校长。

entries.definition: Most important or most successful.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要或最成功的；领先的。

entries.definition: First in order or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 在顺序或重要性上居首的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from strength, becomes an adjective for what weighs most, and then a noun for the biggest pipe or supply.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从力量出发，先成为指「分量最重」的形容词，再成为指最大管道或供应的名词。

normal.en: Main comes from mægen, strength, so the main thing is the one with the most force behind it.
normal.cn: main 来自 mægen（力量），所以最主要的东西就是背后力量最大的那一个。

normal.en: The same root gives might and may, which still carry the idea of power and possibility.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 might 与 may，它们仍带着力量与可能性的意思。

normal.en: A water main is simply the main pipe, the adjective turned into a noun by dropping the word it described.
normal.cn: water main 就是「主要的管道」，形容词通过省去所修饰的词而变成名词。

normal.en: The mains in British homes is the shared public supply, the central channel that every socket draws from.
normal.cn: 英国家庭说的 the mains 是公共供电，是每个插座都从中取电的中心线路。

normal.en: Main clause and main idea show the adjective doing the same job in grammar and in thought: picking out what carries the weight.
normal.cn: main clause 与 main idea 表明这个形容词在语法和思想里做同一件事：挑出承载重量的部分。

abstract.en: The thickest road on a map is not always the longest, but it is the one the whole region depends on.
abstract.cn: 地图上最粗的那条路未必最长，却是整个地区依赖的那一条。

abstract.en: A single pipe under the street feeds every tap in the block; that hidden centrality is the word's quiet image.
abstract.cn: 街道下的一根管道养活整片街区的每个水龙头；这种看不见的中心性正是这个词安静的意象。

abstract.en: To call something main is to make a judgment about weight, not about size alone.
abstract.cn: 把某物称作 main，是在判断它的分量，而不只是判断它的体积。

examples.en: The main road into the valley was still blocked by snow.
examples.cn: 通往山谷的主路仍被雪堵住。

examples.en: A burst water main flooded the lower street.
examples.cn: 一根爆裂的自来水主管淹没了地势较低的那条街。

examples.en: The ship sailed out into the main at dawn.
examples.cn: 船在黎明时驶向外海。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门」——进城的大门那条路最重要；记住 main 是主要的、主路。

root: 古英语 mægen（力量）经中古英语 main（首要的）而来；同族词 might、may 也出自表示「力量、能力」的日耳曼词根，无可靠拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is greatest weight; from it come the principal channel, the public supply, and the old poetic sense of the open sea.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是分量最重；主要通道、公共供电，以及「大海」的古老诗意都由它分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the thickest road on a map, with every side road branching off it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上最粗的那条路，所有岔路都从它分出去。

branches.en: the widest road on a hand-drawn map
branches.cn: 手绘地图上最宽的那条路

branches.en: a buried pipe feeding every tap on the street

normal.en: Mainly because and mainly due to are the two phrases that show the adverb ranking a reason.

senses.title: The heavier side of a comparison: more important
senses.titleCN: 比较中更重的一侧：更重要
senses.definition: more important, more powerful, or more effective than other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中更重要、更有力量或更有效
senses.example: Tourism is a major source of income for the island.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这个岛的主要收入来源。
senses.why: Latin maior is the comparative of magnus 'great'. The word begins as a weighing: two things are compared and one side is heavier. Importance is the first thing this comparison measures, before size or number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maior 是 magnus“大”的比较级。这个词的起点是一次称量：两样东西相比，有一侧更重。这个比较最先量的是重要性，然后才是尺寸或数量。

senses.title: Greater in scale or quantity
senses.definition: larger in size, number, or extent when measured against others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他事物相比，在尺寸、数量或范围上更大
senses.example: A major portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的一大部分用于工资。
senses.why: The same scale now reads quantity rather than rank. Because maior already carries 'more', careful English does not say 'very major': a big city can be a major city, but major itself never means merely big.
senses.whyCN: 同一架天平现在量的是数量而不是位次。由于 maior 本身已含“更多”，规范的英语不说 very major：大城市可以是 major city，但 major 本身从不只表示“尺寸大”。

senses.title: Serious enough to matter: medical and risk use
senses.titleCN: 重大到需要重视：医疗与风险用法
senses.definition: serious in effect or risk, especially of surgery, illness, damage, or change
senses.definitionCN: 在后果或风险上严重，尤用于手术、疾病、损害或变化
senses.example: The patient needs major surgery on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人需要接受膝关节大手术。
senses.why: In medicine the comparison is between procedures that threaten the body and those that do not. A major operation is not simply bigger; it carries a higher risk, so the comparative becomes a judgement of severity.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，比较的两端是威胁身体的手术与不威胁身体的手术。大手术不只是“更大”，而是风险更高，因此比较级变成了一种严重程度的判断。

senses.title: Music: the scale a half-step greater
senses.definition: of a scale, key, or chord built on a major third, sounding brighter and more stable than the minor
senses.definitionCN: 指以大三级为基础的音阶、调或和弦，听感比小调明亮、稳定
senses.example: The piece moves from a minor key into a bright major key.
senses.exampleCN: 这首曲子从小调转入明亮的大调。
senses.why: Music borrowed the word in the 1690s because a major interval is a half-step 'greater' than the minor one. The comparison is now measured on the keyboard rather than on a scale of importance.
senses.whyCN: 音乐在 17 世纪 90 年代借用这个词，因为大三度比小三度“多”一个半音。此时比较是在键盘上量的，而不是在重要性的尺度上量的。

senses.title: University: the subject weighted most
senses.definition: the main subject a student specializes in, or to specialize in that subject
senses.definitionCN: 学生专攻的主修科目，或专攻该科目
senses.example: She majored in economics and minored in statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 她主修经济学，辅修统计学。
senses.why: A degree is a set of subjects, and one of them is weighted more heavily than the rest. The noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890 and the verb by 1910, both keeping the heavier side of the balance.
senses.whyCN: 一个学位由若干科目组成，其中一门的分量重于其余。名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，动词义记录于 1910 年，两者都保留了天平上更重的那一侧。

senses.title: Military rank: the senior officer
senses.definition: an officer rank above captain and below lieutenant colonel
senses.definitionCN: 高于上尉、低于中校的军官军衔
senses.example: The major briefed the company commanders before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 少校在黎明前向各连长做了简报。
senses.why: The rank came through French major, short for sergent-major, from Medieval Latin major 'chief officer'. In a body of officers one is marked as the senior one, so the comparative is used as a title.
senses.whyCN: 这个军衔经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）来自中世纪拉丁语 major“首席军官”。在一群军官中有一人被标为资历更高者，于是比较级被用作头衔。

senses.title: Legal adulthood: the older side of the line
senses.titleCN: 法定成年：年龄界线另一侧的人
senses.definition: a person who has reached the age of legal adulthood, or the state of being of full legal age
senses.definitionCN: 已达到法定成年年龄的人，或处于完全法定成年状态
senses.example: A minor cannot sign the contract; a major can.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人不能签这份合同，成年人可以。
senses.why: Medieval Latin major also named 'an elder, an adult'. Law needs a line between those who can bind themselves and those who cannot, and major marks the person on the older side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 major 也指“年长者、成年人”。法律需要在能为自己负责与不能负责的人之间划一条线，major 标记的就是这条线年长一侧的人。

senses.title: The top tier: major leagues and the majors
senses.titleCN: 最高层级：大联盟与顶级行列
senses.definition: in sport and business, the highest level of competition or the largest organizations, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在体育与商业中，最高级别的赛事或最大的机构，常用复数
senses.example: He spent six seasons in the majors before returning to coach.
senses.exampleCN: 他在顶级联赛打了六个赛季，之后回去当教练。
senses.why: Major league is recorded in baseball by 1892. The comparison now runs between leagues rather than people: one circuit is the greater one, and 'the majors' became shorthand for the top tier in any field.
senses.whyCN: major league 在棒球中记录于 1892 年。此时比较发生在联盟之间而不是人之间：有一个联盟是“更大”的，于是 the majors 成了任何领域顶级行列的简称。

senses.title: Usage boundary: major is not simply big
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：major 不等于“尺寸大”
senses.definition: major describes importance or seriousness rather than physical size alone; it is not graded with very, and minor is its usual opposite
senses.definitionCN: major 描述重要性或严重性，而不只是物理尺寸；它不用 very 分级，其通常的反义词是 minor
senses.example: The storm caused major delays, though the airport itself is not very big.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成了严重延误，尽管机场本身并不大。
senses.why: Because maior is already a comparative, 'very major' is redundant in careful use. A major city is important, not necessarily large; a big city is large, not necessarily important. Major and minor split one scale into two sides.
senses.whyCN: 由于 maior 已是比较级，规范的用法中 very major 是冗余的。major city 是重要的城市，不一定面积大；big city 是面积大的城市，不一定重要。major 与 minor 把同一把尺子分成两侧。

intro.en: Major is the comparative form of the Latin word for 'great'. It entered English around 1300 as a word of rank, and later spread to quantity, music, universities, armies and leagues — always marking the heavier side of a comparison.
intro.cn: major 是拉丁语“大”的比较级形式。它约在 1300 年进入英语，最初表示位次高低，后来扩展到数量、音乐、大学、军队和联赛——始终标记比较中更重的一侧。

items.en: First recorded in English as majour, 'greater, more important or effective, leading, principal'. From c. 1300 it also named an elder or an adult.
items.cn: 最早以 majour 记录于英语，意为“更大的、更重要的或更有效的、领先的、主要的”。约 1300 年起也指年长者或成年人。

items.en: From Latin maior (earlier *magios), the irregular comparative of magnus 'large, great'. A comparative built on a suppletive stem, not on a regular -ior suffix added to magnus.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maior（更早作 *magios），是 magnus“大”的不规则比较级。它是建立在异干互补词干上的比较级，并不是在 magnus 后加规则的 -ior。

items.en: magnus and maior are traced to PIE *meg- 'great', the same root behind magnify, magnitude and master. This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: magnus 与 maior 被追溯到原始印欧语 *meg-“大”，也是 magnify、magnitude、master 的词根。这一重构属于一般认为，而非确证。

items.en: The sense 'greater in quantity, number, or extent' is recorded from the 1590s, extending the comparison from rank to measurable scale.
items.cn: “数量、数目或范围更大”的义项记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，把比较从位次扩展到可测量的规模。

items.en: The military rank appears in the 1640s via French major, short for sergent-major. The musical sense follows in the 1690s, from the idea of an interval a half-step 'greater' than the minor.
items.cn: 军衔义在 17 世纪 40 年代经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）出现。音乐义随后在 17 世纪 90 年代出现，来自“比小调音程多半音”的观念。

items.en: The academic noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890, major league by 1892, and the verb 'to focus one's studies' by 1910 in American English.
items.cn: 学术名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，major league 记录于 1892 年，动词义“专注学业”记录于 1910 年，属美式英语。

note.en: The first group shares the maior / magnus line or looks close to it. The second group separates words for rank, importance, size and degree, which English often uses interchangeably and often should not.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maior／magnus 这条线，或词形接近。第二组区分位次、重要性、尺寸与程度——英语常把它们混用，而很多时候不该混用。

entries.definition: the larger number or part; also the age of legal adulthood. It is the noun built on maior, not a synonym of major.
entries.definitionCN: 多数、较大部分；也指法定成年年龄。它是建立在 maior 上的名词，不是 major 的同义词。

entries.definition: the elected head of a city. It came through French maire from Latin maior 'greater, chief', so it is a cousin, not a derivative of English major.
entries.definitionCN: 民选市长。它经法语 maire 来自拉丁语 maior“更大、首领”，因此是远亲，而不是英语 major 的派生词。

entries.definition: grand and impressive in appearance. It comes from majesty, from Latin maiestas, built on the same maior 'greater' stem.
entries.definitionCN: 外观宏伟、威严的。它来自 majesty，再上溯拉丁语 maiestas，同样建立在 maior“更大”的词干上。

entries.definition: largest or most important among several. It is close to major but usually points to one clear leader, as in the main reason.
entries.definitionCN: 在若干者中最大或最重要的。它接近 major，但通常指向一个明确的领头者，如 the main reason。

entries.definition: highest in rank or authority. It stresses position at the top of a hierarchy, while major stresses weight in a comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 位次或权力最高的。它强调层级顶端的位置，而 major 强调比较中的分量。

entries.definition: first in importance, especially of a reason, aim, or sum. It is more formal and narrower than major.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的，尤用于理由、目标或款项。它比 major 更正式，适用范围更窄。

entries.definition: large or important enough to be noticed or to matter. It can measure degree where major measures rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或重要到值得注意、值得当回事。它可量程度，而 major 量位次。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maior is the comparative of magnus, and the same 'great' stem runs through majority, majesty, magnify, magnitude and master.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maior 是 magnus 的比较级，同一条“大”词干贯穿 majority、majesty、magnify、magnitude、master。

normal.en: maior is a comparative, so major always implies 'than the other one'. A major road matters more than a minor road, not because it is wider.
normal.cn: maior 是比较级，所以 major 总隐含“比另一个更……”。主干道比次要道路重要，不是因为它更宽。

normal.en: magnus 'great' gives magnify, magnitude and magnate; maior gives major, majority and majesty. One family, two stems.
normal.cn: magnus“大”给出 magnify、magnitude、magnate；maior 给出 major、majority、majesty。同一个家族，两条词干。

normal.en: The academic major is the subject given the most weight in a degree, which is why the same word also means 'the important one'.
normal.cn: 大学的 major 是学位中分量最重的科目，这也是同一个词又表示“重要的那一个”的原因。

normal.en: A major in the army is the senior officer in a group, and a legal major is the older person across the age line: both are the 'greater' side.
normal.cn: 军队里的 major 是一群军官中资历更高者，法律上的 major 是年龄界线另一侧的年长者：两者都是“更大”的那一侧。

normal.en: Major league and the majors keep the comparison between leagues: the top circuit is the greater one.
normal.cn: major league 与 the majors 保留的是联盟之间的比较：顶级联盟就是“更大”的那一个。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with two pans. Whatever is placed in them, major names the pan that sinks: more weight, more rank, more risk, more volume.
abstract.cn: 想象一架两端有托盘的天平。无论放进去的是什么，major 指的都是下沉的那一盘：更多分量、更高位次、更大风险、更大体量。

abstract.en: The comparison can be held between cities, keys, subjects, officers or leagues; only the scale changes, never the gesture of weighing.
abstract.cn: 比较可以发生在城市、调式、学科、军官或联盟之间；变的只是尺子，称量这个动作从未改变。

abstract.en: Because one pan is already lower, there is no room to add 'very': the comparison is complete before the adjective is spoken.
abstract.cn: 因为有一盘已经更低，“very”就无处可加：比较在形容词出口之前就已经完成了。

examples.en: Lack of sleep was a major factor in the accident.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足是这起事故的一个主要因素。

examples.en: She majored in history and later became a curator.
examples.cn: 她主修历史，后来成了策展人。

examples.en: The symphony ends in a confident major key.
examples.cn: 这首交响曲在一个自信的大调上结束。

root: 拉丁语 maior“更大的”，是 magnus“大”的比较级，核心是“两者相比更重、更高的一侧”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of major, all one act of weighing: importance, scale, severity, a musical interval, a chosen subject, an officer's rank, legal age, the top league, and the boundary where the word stops meaning 'big'.
sensesIntro.cn: major 的九个义项都出自同一次称量：重要性、规模、严重程度、音程、主修科目、军衔、法定成年、顶级联盟，以及它不再表示“尺寸大”的用法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things are weighed, and major names the heavier pan.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西被称量，major 指更重的那一盘。

branches.en: WEIGHT: importance and quantity are the same comparison read on two different scales.
branches.cn: 分量：重要性与数量是同一场比较在两把不同尺子上的读数。

branches.en: SEVERITY: in medicine the heavier side is the higher risk, so the comparison becomes a warning.
branches.cn: 严重性：在医学里更重的一侧就是更高风险，于是比较变成一种警示。

branches.en: INTERVAL: music measures the greater interval on the keyboard, a half-step above the minor.
branches.cn: 音程：音乐在键盘上量出更大的音程，比小调高一个半音。

branches.en: SELECTION: a chosen subject and a top league are both the item given the most weight in a set.
branches.cn: 选择：主修科目与顶级联盟都是在集合中被赋予最大分量的那一项。

branches.en: RANK, AGE AND BOUNDARY: a senior officer and an adult past the legal line are the greater side of a hierarchy, while the last branch marks the point where major stops meaning 'big'.
branches.cn: 位次、年龄与边界：资历更高的军官与越过法定年龄线的成年人是层级中更大的一侧；最后一条标出 major 不再表示“尺寸大”的分界。

intro.en: Major is not built with a living English prefix. Its Latin stem maior is already a comparative; English only adds noun and adverb suffixes to the finished word.
intro.cn: major 不是用活的英语前缀构成的。它的拉丁词干 maior 本身已是比较级；英语只是在成品词后加名词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family splits into two stems: magnus 'great' (magnify, magnitude) and its comparative maior 'greater' (major, majority, majesty). They are one root seen from two angles.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族分成两条词干：magnus“大”（magnify、magnitude）及其比较级 maior“更大”（major、majority、majesty）。它们是同一个词根的两个视角。

scene: 厨房里灯还亮着，面粉撒在案板上，孩子踮着脚看大人揉面。She made the dough before sunrise and left it covered by the window.

senses.title: To produce or create something
senses.definition: to produce, build or create something out of materials or parts
senses.definitionCN: 用材料或零件做出、建造或创造某物
senses.example: She made a small wooden box for her letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她给信件做了一个小木盒。
senses.why: Old English macian meant to build or fashion, so the first sense is a hand shaping raw material into an object.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 macian 意为建造、塑形，所以第一个义项是手把原料塑成物件。

senses.title: To cause someone or something to be or do something
senses.definition: to cause a person or thing to enter a state or to perform an action
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物进入某种状态，或去做某事
senses.example: The news made everyone quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让所有人都安静下来。
senses.why: Once a hand can shape clay, the same verb is stretched to shaping events: what you do makes a result happen.
senses.whyCN: 既然手能塑造黏土，同一个动词就被延伸到塑造事件：你所做的使某个结果发生。

senses.title: To perform an action
senses.definition: to perform an action, especially one that is named by a noun, such as make a decision or make an effort
senses.definitionCN: 执行某个动作，尤其是由名词命名的动作，如作出决定、付出努力
senses.example: They made a careful decision before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前他们作了慎重的决定。
senses.why: English often pairs a light verb with an action noun, and make is the light verb that turns the noun into something actually done.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把轻动词与动作名词搭配，make 正是那个把名词变成真正做出来的事的轻动词。

senses.title: To earn or gain money
senses.definition: to earn money or gain a profit from work, trade or an investment
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、买卖或投资挣到钱或获得利润
senses.example: The stall made a small profit on its first day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个摊子在开张头一天赚了一点钱。
senses.why: Producing goods that sell turns the verb for making objects into the verb for making money.
senses.whyCN: 把做出来的东西卖出去，就使「制造物件」的动词变成「赚到钱」的动词。

senses.title: The brand of a manufactured product
senses.definition: the brand or particular type under which a product is manufactured and sold
senses.definitionCN: 产品被制造和销售时所标的品牌或特定型号
senses.example: The two cars are the same model but a different make.
senses.exampleCN: 这两辆车是同一款，但品牌不同。
senses.why: A workshop name marked what it turned out, and that mark became the noun for the brand itself.
senses.whyCN: 作坊的名字标示它做出来的东西，这个标记后来就成了指品牌本身的名词。

intro.en: Make is a West Germanic verb for building that widened into causing, performing, earning and the name of a brand.
intro.cn: make 是西日耳曼语中表示建造的动词，后来词义扩展到致使、执行、赚钱以及品牌的名称。

items.en: macian meant to make, build or form, and it was one of the commonest verbs in the language.
items.cn: macian 意为制作、建造、塑形，是当时最常用的动词之一。

items.en: The reconstructed form *makōjanan meant to fashion or put together and is generally taken to be shared with other Germanic verbs of the same meaning.
items.cn: 重构形式 *makōjanan 意为塑形、拼合，一般认为它与其他日耳曼语中同义的动词同出一源。

items.en: macian became maken, and the meaning widened from building to any kind of doing.
items.cn: macian 演变为 maken，词义从建造扩大到各种「做」。

items.en: The pattern make someone do something became ordinary, and so did make in the sense of earning a living.
items.cn: 「让某人做某事」的句式和「谋生、挣钱」的用法在这时都变得平常。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb in hundreds of phrases and adds the noun make for the brand of a product.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个动词留在大量短语里，并添上名词用法，指产品的品牌。

note.cn: 形近组收直接建立在 make 上的形式；近义组收表示使某物产生的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a common Germanic verb for shaping material, and its uses spread from the workshop to causes, actions, wages and brands.

normal.en: Make is the everyday verb for turning material into an object, just as macian was in Old English.
normal.cn: make 是把材料变成物件的日常动词，古英语里的 macian 也是如此。

normal.en: Maker adds -er to make, so the person who makes is simply the verb plus a doer ending.

normal.en: The pattern make him wait is a shortcut: instead of doing the action, you cause someone else to do it.

normal.en: Make a decision sounds strange in some languages, but English uses make as a light verb for actions named by nouns.
normal.cn: 「作出决定」在某些语言里说法不同，但英语把 make 当作轻动词，与名词命名的动作搭配。

normal.en: The noun make for a car brand comes from the workshop mark, not from the act of building.

definition_zh: 管理；掌管；设法做到；勉力完成；应付；对付；靠有限的收入过日子
definition_en: to be in charge of a business or team, to succeed in doing something difficult, to deal with a hard person or situation, or to live on limited means
core_image: 一只手把缰绳一点点收短，躁动的马被稳稳按住
scene: 清晨的马场里，驯马师把缰绳一点点收短，躁动的马终于站定。By evening she was managing the whole stable on her own.
sceneCN: 这里 manage 是「管理、掌管」（第 1 个义项：对一批事务负起责任并决定它如何运转）；句意为到傍晚时，她一个人管着整座马房。图中可辨识物件：收短的缰绳、被按住的马、木栏与草料桶。

pos.zh: 管理；掌管；设法做到；应付；靠有限的钱维持

derivatives.zh: 由 manage 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「管理者；经理」
由 manage 加表示「行为、结果」的后缀 -ment 构成，义为「管理；管理层」
由 manage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「可控制的；对付得了的」
由 manager 加 -ial 构成，义为「管理层的；经营上的」

senses.title: To be in charge of a business or team
senses.definition: to have responsibility for a company, a team or a set of affairs and decide how it should be run
senses.definitionCN: 对一家公司、一支团队或一批事务负起责任，并决定它该如何运转
senses.example: She manages a small team of six engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理着一个由六名工程师组成的小团队。
senses.why: Italian maneggiare first meant to handle a horse with your hands, so the grip on the reins became the grip on a business: control is felt as something held, not merely ordered.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 maneggiare 最初指用手去摆弄、驯服一匹马，于是握住缰绳的那只手后来握住了事务：所谓控制，是被握住的感觉，而不只是发号施令。

senses.title: To succeed in doing something difficult
senses.definition: to succeed in doing something, especially when serious difficulties stand in the way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在明显阻碍之下，仍然把某事做成
senses.example: He managed to finish the report before the power failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他赶在断电之前设法把报告写完了。
senses.why: A handler gets a stubborn animal to move by working it patiently, step after step; the word for handling therefore also means pushing a hard task through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 驯手对付一头犟牲口，是一步又一步耐心摆弄着让它动起来；所以「摆弄」这个词也用来表示把一件难事一路推到做成。

senses.title: To cope with a difficult person or situation
senses.definition: to deal with a difficult person, feeling or situation without losing control of it
senses.definitionCN: 面对难缠的人、情绪或局面，仍能不失控地应对下去
senses.example: She manages difficult customers without ever raising her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她应付难缠的顾客时从不提高嗓门。
senses.why: If managing is keeping a firm hand on something, a difficult customer is only one more thing that must be held steady instead of dropped.
senses.whyCN: 既然管理就是把一件东西稳稳握在手里，那么难缠的顾客也不过是另一件必须稳住、不能松手的东西。

senses.title: To live on limited money or time
senses.titleCN: 靠有限的收入过日子；精打细算
senses.definition: to live or keep going with only a small amount of money or time, using it carefully
senses.definitionCN: 在钱或时间很少的情况下，仔细盘算着维持下去
senses.example: The family manages on one small pension.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人靠一份微薄的养老金过日子。
senses.why: Running a household on little money is the same skill of handling resources, so manage also came to mean stretching whatever is already in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 用很少的钱撑起一个家，仍是同一套摆弄资源的本事，于是 manage 又表示把手里已经有的那点东西拉长来用。

intro.en: Manage reaches English through Italian and French, and the word still smells of the stable: to manage a horse came before managing a company.
intro.cn: manage 经意大利语与法语进入英语，词里至今还留着马房的气味：先会驯马，后来才谈管理公司。

items.en: Manus is the ordinary Latin noun for the hand, and the hand was the ancient image of control over any object.
items.cn: manus 是拉丁语中表示「手」的普通名词，而手一向是「掌控某物」的古老形象。

items.en: Italian kept the Latin noun as mano, still meaning hand, and built its verb of handling on that base.
items.cn: 意大利语把拉丁名词保留为 mano，仍指手，并在这个词基上造出了表示「摆弄」的动词。

items.en: Maneggiare meant to work something with the hands, above all to train and ride a horse in the riding school.
items.cn: maneggiare 意为用手去弄某样东西，其中最主要指在马术学校里驯马、驭马。

items.en: French manège named a riding school and the art taught there; its form and its stable sense pressed on the English borrowing of the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 manège 指马术学校以及在那里教的技艺；它的词形与马房义在十六世纪影响了英语的借入形式。

items.en: Modern English drops the stable and keeps the grip, managing ships, money, staff, crowds and finally a difficult afternoon.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了马房，只留下那只握住的手，用它来管船、管钱、管人、管人群，最后也管一个难熬的下午。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and words built on the Latin noun for hand; the near group gathers verbs for running, handling and coping.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及建立在拉丁语「手」这个名词上的词；近义组收表示经营、处理与应对的动词。

entries.definition: The person who manages a team or a business.
entries.definitionCN: 管理团队或业务的人；由 manage 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The activity of managing, or the people who run a firm.
entries.definitionCN: 管理这项活动；也指经营一家公司的那批人；由 manage 加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Easy enough to control or deal with.
entries.definitionCN: 容易控制或应付的；由 manage 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: Done with the hands, or a handbook of instructions; from Latin manus, hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手做的；也指操作手册；出自拉丁语 manus（手），与 manage 同源。

entries.definition: To handle or control something, often by unfair means.
entries.definitionCN: 摆弄或操控某物，常指用不正当手段；词根同为拉丁语 manus（手）。

entries.definition: To be in charge of and operate a business or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 负责经营一家企业或机构。

entries.definition: To work or control a machine, a system or a business.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器、系统，或经营业务。

entries.definition: To deal with a person, a problem or a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 应付某人、某个问题或某种局面。

entries.definition: To deal successfully with a difficult situation.
entries.definitionCN: 成功应对困难的局面。

entries.definition: To watch over people or work and make sure it is done properly.
entries.definitionCN: 监督人或工作，确保其正常进行。

normalIntro.en: The word grew out of a stable, where managing meant working the reins with your hands, and its family keeps returning to grip, affairs and tasks pushed through.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从马房里长出来，那时的 manage 是用手摆弄缰绳；它的同族词反复回到握持、事务，以及被推到做成的难事。

normal.en: Latin manus means hand, and Italian made maneggiare from mano, so to manage is first to have something in your hand.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，意大利语又用 mano 造出 maneggiare，所以 manage 起初就是把某样东西握在手里。

normal.en: The earliest English sense is to train a horse, which is why a rider's control still sits inside the modern word.
normal.cn: 这个词在英语里最早的意思是驯马，所以骑手那种控制感至今还留在现代词义里。

normal.en: French manège, a riding school, reshaped the borrowed word in the sixteenth century and kept the stable flavour.
normal.cn: 法语 manège 指马术学校，它在十六世纪改塑了这个借词，也留下了马房的气息。

normal.en: Manager adds -er for the person, management adds -ment for the activity, manageable adds -able for what can be handled.
normal.cn: manager 加 -er 指人，management 加 -ment 指活动，manageable 加 -able 指「拿得住、对付得了」。

normal.en: Manage to do keeps the old image: you work the task with your hands until it finally moves.
normal.cn: manage to do 保留着旧画面：你用双手反复摆弄那件事，直到它终于动起来。

abstract.en: Control is pictured as a grip: what you cannot hold, you cannot manage.
abstract.cn: 控制被想象成一次握持：握不住的东西，就管不了。

abstract.en: A horse, a company and a bad afternoon are all things the same hand is asked to steady.
abstract.cn: 一匹马、一家公司、一个难熬的下午，都是同一只手被要求稳住的东西。

abstract.en: The word began in a stable and ended in an office, yet the gesture never changed.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于马房，落于办公室，中间的那个动作却始终没变。

examples.en: The family manages on one small pension.
examples.cn: 这一家人靠一份微薄的养老金过日子。

root: 意大利语 maneggiare（用手摆弄、驯马）出自 mano（手），再上溯到拉丁语 manus（手）；英语在十六世纪借入 manage，并受法语 manège（马术学校）影响。
