definition_zh: 管理；经营；（企业的）管理层；对疾病或局面的处理方式
definition_en: the activity of running and controlling an organization or process, or the people who do it
core_image: 一只手把散在各处的线头收拢，编成一股能拉动的缰绳
scene: 四家分店各做各的账，月底总对不上数，后来同一个人统一排班、定采购、查库存。Careful management brought the four branches onto one schedule.
sceneCN: 这里 management 指把分散的人、钱与流程收在一起加以调度（第 1 个义项：对组织的统筹经营）；句意：细致的管理让四家分店归到同一张时间表上。图中可辨识物件：账本、排班表、货箱、统一的门牌。

pos.zh: 管理；经营；管理层；（对疾病、局面的）处理方式

forms.label: 复数（指多家机构的管理层）

senses.title: Running an organization
senses.titleCN: 把一个组织的各项工作统筹起来
senses.definition: the activity of planning, organizing and controlling the work of an organization so that it runs well
senses.definitionCN: 对一个组织的各项工作加以计划、组织与控制，使其运转良好
senses.example: Good management kept the shipyard busy through the downturn.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的管理让这家船厂在衰退期仍有活干。
senses.why: The word began as handling a horse with the hand, and running a firm is that same gesture applied to people, money and schedules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指用手摆弄、驯服一匹马；经营一家公司，就是把同样的动作施加到人、钱与日程上。

senses.title: The people in charge
senses.definition: the group of senior people who make the main decisions in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织里作出主要决策的高层群体
senses.example: Management agreed to freeze hiring until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 管理层同意把招聘冻结到春天。
senses.why: Once the activity became a permanent job, the people who did it could be spoken of as one body.
senses.whyCN: 当这种活计变成常设职位，做这件事的人就被当作一个整体来说。

senses.title: Skill in handling people
senses.definition: the ability to deal with people and awkward situations without letting them get out of hand
senses.definitionCN: 与人以及棘手局面打交道时不让事情失控的能力
senses.example: It took patient management to keep the two departments speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 要让两个部门继续对话，需要很有耐心的周旋。
senses.why: A rider controls a horse by feel rather than force, and the same word covers handling people by feel.
senses.whyCN: 骑手靠手感而不是蛮力控制马匹，这个词也用来指靠分寸感与人相处。

senses.title: Careful use of resources
senses.titleCN: 对钱财与时间的节制使用
senses.definition: the careful control of money, time or supplies so that nothing is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 对金钱、时间或物资的谨慎支配，使什么也不被浪费
senses.example: Tighter management of the fuel budget halved the depot's winter costs.
senses.exampleCN: 对燃料预算更严格的把控让仓库的冬季开支减半。
senses.why: What the hand holds it can also ration; the horse-training word grew into the sense of not letting a supply run out.
senses.whyCN: 手握得住东西，也就能分配它；驯马那个词由此长出「不让储备用尽」的意思。

senses.title: Medical care over time
senses.titleCN: 对慢性病的长期治疗与监控
senses.definition: the treatment and steady control of a disease or condition, especially one that lasts
senses.definitionCN: 对疾病或身体状况进行治疗与持续控制，尤指长期存在的情况
senses.example: Pain management now includes a weekly check with a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛管理现在包含每周由护士做的一次复查。
senses.why: A doctor who keeps a disease in hand for months is managing it in the same old sense of handling.
senses.whyCN: 医生把一种病在手里管上几个月，用的仍是「用手把控」那个老意思。

senses.title: Control of land and animals
senses.titleCN: 对土地、畜群等自然资源的经营
senses.definition: the control and use of land, animals or natural resources according to a plan
senses.definitionCN: 按计划对土地、牲畜或自然资源加以控制与使用
senses.example: The ranch's grazing management keeps the grass from wearing out.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场的放牧管理让草场不至于被耗尽。
senses.why: Herds and fields were the first things a hand had to manage, so land and livestock keep the oldest layer of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 畜群与田地是手最早要照管的对象，因此土地与牲畜保留了最古老的那层意思。

senses.title: Management as a subject
senses.titleCN: 作为一门学科的管理学
senses.definition: the study of how organizations are run, taught as an academic subject
senses.definitionCN: 研究组织如何运转的学问，作为一门学科来教授
senses.example: He added a management course to his engineering degree.
senses.exampleCN: 他在工程学位之外又加了一门管理课程。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the handling of firms was written down, taught and examined, and so became a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 到了二十世纪，经营企业的门道被写成教材、被教授、被考试，于是成了一门学问。

senses.title: The handling of an event
senses.titleCN: 对某一具体事件或局面的处置
senses.definition: the way a particular problem, crisis or event is dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 对某个具体问题、危机或事件的应对方式
senses.example: The management of the flood response drew criticism from residents.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水应对的处置方式招来了居民的批评。
senses.why: Here the object of handling shrinks from a whole firm to one event, but the gesture itself stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里被把控的对象从整个公司缩小到一桩事件，动作本身没有变。

intro.en: Management is the noun of manage, which came through Italian from Latin manus 'hand'. The modern business sense grew out of handling horses, then households, then firms.
intro.cn: management 是 manage 的名词，而 manage 经意大利语上溯到拉丁 manus「手」；现代企业义由驯马、理家一路扩展到经营公司。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand' and also the power to hold something under control, so handling and controlling were one idea from the start.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」，也指把某物握在控制之下的权力，因此「用手摆弄」与「掌控」从一开始就是一个念头。

items.en: Italian maneggiare, built on mano 'hand', meant to handle an object and especially to train a horse; the horse sense is the one usually cited for the English verb.
items.cn: 意大利语 maneggiare 由 mano「手」构成，指用手操作物件，尤指驯马；英语动词最常被追溯到的是驯马这一义。

items.en: Manage entered English in the sixteenth century, first of handling horses and weapons; management, the noun of the activity, followed in the same period.
items.cn: manage 在十六世纪进入英语，最初用于摆弄马匹与兵器；指这项活动的名词 management 也在同一时期出现。

items.en: French ménager 'to run a household' is generally thought to have strengthened the sense of ordering a household or estate, which later widened to a business.
items.cn: 一般认为法语 ménager「料理家务」强化了「安排家务与产业」这一义，后来再扩大到经营企业。

items.en: The noun suffix -ment, from Latin -mentum through French, names the activity or its result, which is how management came to mean both the doing and the body that does it.
items.cn: 这个名词后缀经法语来自拉丁语中表示动作或结果的后缀，management 因此既指「做这件事」，也指「做这件事的那群人」。

items.en: The first recorded dates for the business and academic senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 企业义与学科义的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十六世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like management; the second group names neighbouring ways of running something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 management 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「经营、支配」说法。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; it keeps the plain action of handling a firm or a horse.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，保留「摆弄、经营一家公司或一匹马」的直白动作。

entries.definition: The person who performs the activity, formed with the agent suffix; it is not the activity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做这件事的人，由施动后缀构成，不是这项活动本身。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything connected with managers or their methods.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述与管理者或管理方法有关的事物。

entries.definition: A riding school, from the same Italian word for handling horses; the link is the stable, not the office.
entries.definitionCN: 指马术学校，同出那个表示驯马的意大利词；联系在马厩，而不在办公室。

entries.definition: From Latin manica 'sleeve, handcuff', also built on manus, but it names a restraint rather than a skill.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 manica「袖子、手铐」，同样由 manus 构成，但指束缚之物，不是经营的本事。

entries.definition: The running of an institution according to its rules; it stresses procedure more than direction.
entries.definitionCN: 按规章维持机构运转，强调程序多过掌舵。

entries.definition: The system by which an organization is directed and held accountable, rather than the daily work of running it.
entries.definitionCN: 指组织被引导并接受问责的制度，而非日常经营的具体事务。

entries.definition: Careful, responsible handling of money or resources left in one's charge.
entries.definitionCN: 对受托的钱财资源做审慎负责的照管。

entries.definition: Authority to direct something; it names the power, while management names the whole activity.
entries.definitionCN: 支配某事的权力；它指权力本身，management 指整套活动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Manus is Latin for hand, so management is literally handling.
normal.cn: manus 是拉丁语「手」，management 字面上就是「用手摆弄、照管」。

normal.en: The family runs manage, manager, managerial, manageable and mismanagement.
normal.cn: 同族词有 manage、manager、managerial、manageable 与 mismanagement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: time management, crisis management, top management.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：时间管理、危机处理、高层管理层。

normal.en: The noun suffix -ment turns the act of managing into the thing called management.
normal.cn: 名词后缀把「管理」这个动作变成名为 management 的事物。

normal.en: Italian maneggiare first meant to train a horse by hand, which is the oldest picture in the word.
normal.cn: 意大利语 maneggiare 最初指用手驯马，这是这个词里最古老的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on four loose threads at once and pulling them into one line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手一次攥住四根散线，把它们拉成一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a rider who never pulls hard, only shifts weight, and the whole herd follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一位从不猛拉缰绳、只挪动重心的骑手，整群马都跟着走。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where every paper is already filed before anyone asks for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，别人还没开口要，每份纸就已经归好了位。

examples.en: Local clinics improved their management of patient records last year.
examples.cn: 本地诊所去年改善了对病人档案的管理。

examples.en: The management of the harbour was split between two agencies.
examples.cn: 港口的经营权被分给了两个机构。

examples.en: She studied management after six years on the factory floor.
examples.cn: 在车间干了六年后，她去攻读管理学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「man（人）+ age（年纪）+ ment（名词）」——管人管到上年纪，就是管理

root: 拉丁 manus「手」→ 意大利 maneggiare「用手操作、驯马」→ 法语 ménager「料理家务」→ 英语 manage「管理」；末尾是名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand: it runs a firm, becomes a body of managers, handles people, rations supplies, holds a disease in check, works land and herds, turns into a taught subject, and finally grips a single event.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一只手：经营一家公司、聚成一群管理者、应对人、分配物资、把病管住、照料土地与畜群、变成一门被教授的学问，最后攥住一桩具体事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand gathers loose threads and pulls them into a single rein.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把散开的线头收拢，拉成一根缰绳。

branches.en: THE HAND ITSELF: planning, organizing and controlling a whole firm is the original gesture at full size.
branches.cn: 手本身：对一个公司作计划、组织与控制，就是最初那个动作放到最大。

branches.en: WHO HOLDS THE REIN: the handlers become a standing body, and their feel for people becomes a skill.
branches.cn: 谁握着缰绳：做事的人聚成常设群体，他们待人的手感变成一种本事。

branches.en: WHAT IS RATIONED: the hand decides how much fuel, time or money may leave the store.
branches.cn: 被分配的东西：手决定有多少燃料、时间或钱可以从库里出去。

branches.en: CARE OVER TIME: a disease and a pasture are both kept in condition by regular attention.
branches.cn: 长期的照料：疾病与牧场都靠按时看顾才维持在可用状态。

branches.en: FROM PRACTICE TO OBJECT: the habit is written down as a subject, or narrowed to one event.
branches.cn: 从做法变成对象：这套习惯被写成学科，或被收窄到一桩事件上。

intro.en: Management is built from a Latin hand and a noun suffix, and the hand also supports several English words.
intro.cn: management 由一个拉丁语「手」和一个名词后缀构成，这个「手」还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manacle and mandate; the Italian verb maneggiare gives manage and its English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 manus 衍生 manual（手册）、manacle（手铐）与 mandate（委托）；意大利语 maneggiare 衍生 manage 及其英语词族。

items.example: The root supplies the picture of a hand on a rein.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「手握缰绳」的画面。

items.meaning: to handle; to train a horse
items.example: The stable sense is the oldest source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 马厩里的这一义是英语词最早的来源。

items.example: One hand can manage a horse, a household or a firm.
items.exampleCN: 一只手可以管马、理家，也可以管公司。

items.meaning: the activity of running; the managers
items.example: The suffix turns the deed into the thing named.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动作变成被命名的事物。

items.meaning: the person who runs the work
items.example: The agent suffix names the hand that holds the rein.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀点出握缰的那只手。

items.example: The adjective describes the hand's work, not the hand.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述手的活儿，而不是手本身。

items.example: What can be held in one hand is manageable.
items.exampleCN: 一只手握得住的东西就是可控的。

items.example: The prefix says the hand gripped the rein the wrong way.
items.exampleCN: 前缀说明这只手握错了缰绳。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It is the same ending as in agreement and movement.
items.exampleCN: 它与「同意」「移动」两个词用的是同一个词尾。

latinEntries.meaning: to put into someone's hand; entrust

definition_zh: 经理；管理者；球队或乐队的事务负责人；某项事务的专责人
definition_en: a person whose job is to organize and control the work of a business, team or activity
core_image: 缰绳从一只手伸向前方，前后都是一队等着被安排的人
scene: 演出前一天设备出了故障，那个人逐个打电话借音箱、改场地、重排时间。A manager solves problems before the audience notices.
sceneCN: 这里 manager 指为一项活动统筹人、事与资源的人（第 1 个义项：负责机构或团队运转的人）；句意：一位经理在观众察觉之前就把问题解决掉。图中可辨识物件：音箱、改期通知、场地平面图、装设备的木箱。

pos.zh: 经理；管理者；事务负责人

senses.title: The person who runs a business
senses.titleCN: 掌管一家企业或团队的人
senses.definition: a person employed to run a business, a team or a group of workers
senses.definitionCN: 受雇掌管一家企业、一支团队或一群工人的人
senses.example: The manager of the repair shop orders parts and sets the rota.
senses.exampleCN: 修理店的经理负责订零件、排班表。
senses.why: Manager is the noun of the hand that holds the rein, so it names whoever keeps the whole body of work moving.
senses.whyCN: manager 是握缰那只手的名词形式，指让全部工作继续转动的那个人。

senses.title: Head of one department
senses.definition: the person who heads a single department or function within a larger organization
senses.definitionCN: 在较大机构中主管某一个部门或职能的人
senses.example: The sales manager reports to the regional director.
senses.exampleCN: 销售经理向区域总监汇报。
senses.why: One department is a single rein of the firm, and its head pulls only that one.
senses.whyCN: 一个部门只是公司的一根缰绳，它的负责人只拉这一根。

senses.title: Boss of a sports team
senses.titleCN: 运动队的领队或主教练
senses.definition: the person who picks the players and directs a team during matches
senses.definitionCN: 挑选球员并在比赛中指挥球队的人
senses.example: The manager changed formation after the first goal.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个球之后，主教练换了阵型。
senses.why: The Italian verb behind the word was used of training horses, so a team boss keeps the oldest sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的意大利语动词用于驯马，因此球队主帅保留了最古老的那层意思。

senses.title: Business agent for performers
senses.titleCN: 艺人或乐队的事务代理人
senses.definition: someone who handles contracts, bookings and money for a performer or group
senses.definitionCN: 替艺人或团体处理合同、演出安排与收入的人
senses.example: Her manager turned down the film offer on her behalf.
senses.exampleCN: 她的经纪人替她推掉了那部电影的邀约。
senses.why: A performer needs someone to handle contracts the way a rider handles the direction of a horse.
senses.whyCN: 艺人需要有人替他打理合同，就像骑手替马把握方向。

senses.title: Someone who looks after another's money or property
senses.titleCN: 替他人打理钱财产业的人
senses.definition: a person employed to look after money, land or property for its owner
senses.definitionCN: 受雇替业主照管钱财、土地或房产的人
senses.example: The estate manager hires the gardeners and pays the bills.
senses.exampleCN: 产业经理雇请园丁，并支付各项账单。
senses.why: Money and land are things a hand holds on another's behalf, so the handler is named after the hand.
senses.whyCN: 钱财与土地是手替别人握着的东西，因此这个代管者以「手」来命名。

senses.title: A program that organizes things
senses.titleCN: 整理文件或窗口的计算机程序
senses.definition: a piece of software that organizes files, windows or settings
senses.definitionCN: 整理文件、窗口或设置的软件
senses.example: The download manager keeps the parts in order.
senses.exampleCN: 下载管理器把各个分段按顺序放好。
senses.why: Software does by rule what a hand did by feel: it keeps the pieces sorted in their places.
senses.whyCN: 软件用规则去做手凭手感做的事：把各个零碎归到各自的位置。

senses.title: The person in charge of one project
senses.titleCN: 某一项目的专责负责人
senses.definition: the person responsible for one project from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 从头到尾对某一个项目负责的人
senses.example: The project manager moved the launch back by a month.
senses.exampleCN: 项目经理把上线日期往后推了一个月。
senses.why: A project is one bounded task, and its manager holds only that task until it is finished.
senses.whyCN: 一个项目是一项有边界的工作，项目经理只管这一件，直到它完成。

senses.title: The person in charge of a shop
senses.titleCN: 一家店铺的现场负责人
senses.definition: the person who runs a single shop or branch day to day
senses.definitionCN: 日复一日经营一家店铺或分店的人
senses.example: The store manager counts the till before locking up.
senses.exampleCN: 门店经理在锁门前清点收银账目。
senses.why: A shop is a small ring of work, and one person keeps that ring turning every day.
senses.whyCN: 一家店是一个小小的循环，一个人每天让它转起来。

intro.en: Manager adds the agent suffix to manage, a word that came from Italian horse handling. The role names grew apart as firms, clubs and estates each needed a handler.
intro.cn: manager 在 manage 之后加上施动后缀；manage 来自意大利语的驯马行话。随着公司、俱乐部与产业各自需要有人打理，这个称呼分化出不同角色。

items.en: Manus 'hand' also carried the idea of control, which is why a handler and a controller share one root.
items.cn: manus「手」同时带有掌控之意，因此「动手的人」与「掌控的人」共用同一个词根。

items.en: Maneggiare meant to handle and especially to train a horse; the trainer of horses is the oldest kind of manager.
items.cn: maneggiare 指用手操作，尤指驯马；驯马人就是最古老的一类管理者。

items.en: Manage is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, and manager, the one who manages, from the late sixteenth century; both dates are approximate.
items.cn: manage 在十六世纪见于英语记录，指做这件事的 manager 则见于十六世纪晚期；两个年代都是约数。

items.en: The Old English suffix -er marks the doer of an action, so manager is literally the handling one.
items.cn: 古英语的施动后缀标记动作的执行者，因此 manager 字面上就是「动手打理的那一个」。

items.en: Sports clubs, theatres and country estates gave the word its separate everyday roles in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 体育俱乐部、剧院与乡间产业在十八、十九世纪分别赋予这个词不同的日常角色。

note.en: The first group shares shape or root with manager; the second group names other people who direct work.
note.cn: 第一组与 manager 共享形音或词根；第二组是其他指挥工作的人。

entries.definition: The verb, naming the action rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指动作而不是人。

entries.definition: The activity or the whole body of managers, not one individual.
entries.definitionCN: 指这项活动或整个管理层，不是单个个人。

entries.definition: A riding school, from the same Italian word for handling horses.
entries.definitionCN: 马术学校，同出那个表示驯马的意大利词。

entries.definition: From Dutch manneken 'little man'; the shared shape is accidental, and it names a dummy.
entries.definitionCN: 来自荷兰语 manneken「小人」；形似只是巧合，它指服装模特或假人。

entries.definition: One who watches over workers directly; the emphasis is on checking, not on running the whole unit.
entries.definitionCN: 直接看管工人的人，强调检查，而不是经营整个单元。

entries.definition: One who runs an institution's procedures and records; the focus is rules and paper.
entries.definitionCN: 维持机构程序与记录的人，重心在规章与文书。

entries.definition: A member of the top board or the head of a whole organization.
entries.definitionCN: 董事会成员或整个机构的负责人。

entries.definition: An informal word for whoever gives orders; it says nothing about handling work well.
entries.definitionCN: 指发号施令者的口语词，并不含「把工作打理得好」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real word family and real job titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的职位名称。

normal.en: Manus is hand, and -er is the doer, so manager is the one with a hand on the work.
normal.cn: manus 是手，施动后缀指做事的人，manager 就是那只按在工作上的手。

normal.en: The family runs manage, management, managerial and managership.
normal.cn: 同族词有 manage、management、managerial 与 managership。

normal.en: Real titles show the spread: store manager, project manager, sales manager.
normal.cn: 真实职位显示它的分布：门店经理、项目经理、销售经理。

normal.en: The oldest picture is a horse trainer, because the Italian verb meant exactly that.
normal.cn: 最古老的画面是驯马人，因为那个意大利语动词本就是这个意思。

normal.en: A manager is measured by the work that keeps moving, not by tasks done personally.
normal.cn: 衡量一位经理的，是继续运转的工作，而不是他亲手做完的活儿。

abstract.en: Picture a stagehand who fixes a broken light while the curtain is still closed.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布还没拉开，一名舞台工作人员已经把坏掉的灯修好。

abstract.en: Picture a rider who steers with the knees and leaves both hands free.
abstract.cn: 想象一位用膝盖控向、腾出双手的骑手。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing at the joint of four pipes, turning each valve a little.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在四根管道的接合处，把每个阀门都拧一点。

examples.en: The branch manager rewrote the rota so nobody worked six days straight.
examples.cn: 分店经理重排了班表，没人再连上六天。

examples.en: A good manager knows which decisions can wait until Monday.
examples.cn: 好的管理者知道哪些决定可以等到周一再做。

examples.en: The band's manager cancelled the tour rather than cut the fee.
examples.cn: 乐队经纪人宁可取消巡演，也不肯压低酬劳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「man（人）+ ager（上年纪的人）」——公司里管人又上了年纪的那位，就是经理

root: 拉丁 manus「手」→ 意大利 maneggiare「驯马、操作」→ 英语 manage「管理」+ 施动后缀「做事的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand from a whole firm down to a single shop: the general runner, a department head, a team boss, an agent for another, a keeper of property, a sorting program, one project and one counter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一只手，从整个公司缩小到一家店铺：总管、部门负责人、球队主帅、代他人打理事务者、产业代管人、整理文件的程序、单个项目、一个柜台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand on the rein, with a line of people and tasks behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着缰绳，身后是一队人与一列待办的事。

branches.en: THE WHOLE REIN: the general manager holds every part of the business at once.
branches.cn: 整根缰绳：总经理同时握住企业的每一部分。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF CAPTAIN: one leads a department, the other leads players.
branches.cn: 两种带队人：一个带部门，一个带球员。

branches.en: ACTING FOR ANOTHER: an agent handles a career, an estate manager handles property.
branches.cn: 代他人出手：经纪人打理职业生涯，产业经理打理房产。

branches.en: ORGANIZING INSTRUMENTS: software sorts files, a project lead sorts tasks.
branches.cn: 整理的工具：软件归置文件，项目负责人归置任务。

branches.en: ONE SMALL RING: a single shop is the smallest circle a manager keeps turning.
branches.cn: 最小的循环：一家店铺是经理让它转动的最小一圈。

intro.en: Manager is a Latin-rooted verb plus an English agent suffix, and the same root reaches several everyday words.
intro.cn: manager 是一个拉丁词根的动词加上英语施动后缀，这个词根还通向若干日常词。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manacle and mandate; the Italian verb gives manage and its English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 manus 衍生 manual、manacle 与 mandate；意大利语动词衍生 manage 及其英语词族。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供握持工作的那只手。

definition_zh: 方式；方法；举止；态度；礼貌；礼节；风格；手法
definition_en: the way in which something is done, a person's bearing towards others, polite social behaviour in the plural, or a recognizable style in art
core_image: 同一只手，握杯子时轻，握锤子时重，落下的力道各不相同
scene: 画室的长桌上摆着同一只杯子的三幅画稿，每一幅落笔的轻重都不一样。He stirred the paint in a slow, deliberate manner before the first stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 manner 是「方式、方法」（第 1 个义项：做某件事时所采取的样子）；句意为他在落第一笔之前，以缓慢而有意的方式搅动颜料。图中可辨识物件：三幅杯子画稿、颜料碟、长桌。

pos.zh: 方式；方法；举止；态度；礼貌；风格

derivatives.zh: 由 manner 加表示「做法、主义」的后缀 -ism 构成，义为「习惯性的小动作；（艺术上的）风格主义」
由 manner 加 -ly 构成，义为「有礼貌的；举止得体的」
由 manner 加 -ed 构成，义为「举止不自然的；做作的」

senses.title: The way something is done
senses.definition: the way in which something is done, happens or is arranged
senses.definitionCN: 某事被做、发生或安排时所呈现的样子
senses.example: She answered every question in a calm, even manner that quieted the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她以平静而匀称的方式回答每一个问题，让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: The word descends from Latin manus, hand; manner is literally the way a thing is handled, so the shape of the doing is what it names first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 manus（手）；manner 字面上就是「一样东西被手握持的样子」，所以它最先命名的就是做事的形状。

senses.title: A person's bearing towards others
senses.definition: the way a person behaves, speaks or carries themselves in front of other people
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在他人面前表现、说话、举手投足的样子
senses.example: His easy manner made strangers feel they had known him for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他随和的举止让陌生人觉得已经认识他多年。
senses.why: Handling a person is as physical as handling an object, so the way you hold yourself in company also became a manner.
senses.whyCN: 待人接物和处理物件一样带着身体感，于是你在人前拿住自己的那种姿态，也成了一种 manner。

senses.title: Polite social behaviour, chiefly in the plural
senses.definition: the polite habits and rules of behaviour that a society expects, usually used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会所期待的那套礼貌习惯与行为规矩，通常以复数出现
senses.example: The children were taught to mind their manners at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被教导在餐桌旁要讲究礼貌。
senses.why: One manner is a single way of acting; once a society agrees on the approved ways, they are counted up as manners, and the plural marks a set of rules.
senses.whyCN: 单个 manner 是一种做法；一旦社会就「哪些做法被认可」达成一致，它们就被一条条数出来成了 manners，复数标出的是一整套规矩。

senses.title: A recognizable style in art or writing
senses.definition: the personal or period style that marks a work of art, writing or music
senses.definitionCN: 标在一件艺术品、文字或音乐上的个人风格或时代风格
senses.example: The late portraits were painted in the manner of his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 那些晚期肖像是以他旧日老师的手法画成的。
senses.why: If manner is the way a hand moves, a painter's repeated handling of paint is recognized as that painter's manner, and style follows from the same observation.
senses.whyCN: 如果 manner 是一只手动作的样子，那么一位画家反复处理颜料的方式就会被人认作他的 manner，「风格」的意思便从同一种观察里长出来。

intro.en: Manner comes from a Latin adjective built on the word for hand, and it passed through French before English used it for ways, bearing, politeness and style.
intro.cn: manner 出自一个建立在「手」这个词上的拉丁形容词，经法语中转之后，才在英语里用来指方式、举止、礼貌与风格。

items.en: Manus, the Latin noun for hand, supplied the base for a whole family of words about handling and the way things are held.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 manus 意为手，为了一整族关于摆弄以及握持方式的词提供了词基。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin adjective manuarius, of the hand, is generally taken as the link; it described what belongs to the hand or the way it holds something.
items.cn: 一般认为俗拉丁语形容词 manuarius（手的）是中间环节；它描述属于手的，或手握持某物的方式。

items.en: Old French maniere meant way, sort or kind, and it carried the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 maniere 意为方式、种类，在诺曼时期之后把这个词带进英语。

items.en: Middle English maner covered way, custom and behaviour, and the modern spelling manner settled later under French influence.
items.cn: 中古英语 maner 兼指方式、习俗与行为，现代拼写 manner 后来在法语影响下固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps manner for ways and bearing, counts the plural manners as polite behaviour, and lets art criticism use it for a personal stroke.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 manner 指方式与举止，把复数 manners 用作礼貌行为，也让艺术评论用它指个人的笔法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and words built on the Latin noun for hand; the near group gathers nouns for ways of doing and ways of carrying oneself.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及建立在拉丁语「手」这个名词上的词；近义组收表示做事方式与自我呈现方式的名称。

entries.definition: A habitual gesture or way of speaking, or an exaggerated style in art.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性的动作或说话方式；也指艺术上夸张做作的风格；由 manner 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: Showing good manners; polite.
entries.definitionCN: 有礼貌的；举止得体的；由 manner 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Behaving in an artificial or exaggerated way.
entries.definitionCN: 举止做作、不自然的；由 manner 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Done with the hands, or a handbook; from Latin manus, hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手做的；也指手册；出自拉丁语 manus（手），与 manner 同源。

entries.definition: The method or style in which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事所采用的方法或样式。

entries.definition: A planned and regular way of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划、有步骤的做事方式。

entries.definition: A distinctive way of doing, writing or designing.
entries.definitionCN: 独特的做事、写作或设计方式。

entries.definition: The way a person stands, moves or carries themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人站立、走动或自我呈现的姿态。

entries.definition: The outward behaviour and appearance a person shows to others.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人在他人面前表现出的外在举止与神情。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin noun for hand, and its family keeps returning to handling, bearing, social rules and the personal stroke of an artist.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「手」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到握持、姿态、社交规矩，以及艺术家的个人笔法。

normal.en: Latin manus means hand, and the Vulgar Latin manuarius, of the hand, is the usual link to French maniere, a way or kind.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，俗拉丁语 manuarius（手的）通常是通向法语 maniere（方式、种类）的中间环节。

normal.en: Manner is therefore the look of a thing being handled, which explains why it can name a method and a bearing at once.
normal.cn: 所以 manner 就是「一样东西被握持时的样子」，这解释了它为何既能指方法，又能指姿态。

normal.en: Manners became a separate plural word because polite behaviour is learned as a set of approved ways.
normal.cn: manners 成为独立的复数词，是因为礼貌行为是作为一整套被认可的做法学来的。

normal.en: Mannerism and mannerly both grow straight out of manner, one naming a habit, the other naming good behaviour.
normal.cn: mannerism 与 mannerly 都直接从 manner 长出来，一个指习惯动作，一个指得体的举止。

normal.en: The phrase in a manner of speaking marks the method sense, softened into a polite hedge.
normal.cn: 短语 in a manner of speaking 标出了「方式」这层意思，又被磨成一句客气的退让。

abstract.en: A hand's pressure is never twice the same, and that difference is what the word first names.
abstract.cn: 一只手落下的力道从不完全相同，而这点差别正是这个词最先命名的东西。

abstract.en: Method, bearing and politeness are one idea at three distances: how a thing is held, how a body is held, how a self is held.
abstract.cn: 方法、姿态与礼貌是同一个念头在三个距离上：东西怎么被握，身体怎么被摆，自己怎么被端住。

abstract.en: Style is only manner that has become recognizable enough to carry a name.
abstract.cn: 风格不过是已经明显到足以拥有名字的那种 manner。

examples.en: She answered every question in a calm, even manner that quieted the room.
examples.cn: 她以平静而匀称的方式回答每一个问题，让整个房间安静下来。

examples.en: The children were taught to mind their manners at the table.
examples.cn: 孩子们被教导在餐桌旁要讲究礼貌。

examples.en: The late portraits were painted in the manner of his old teacher.
examples.cn: 那些晚期肖像是以他旧日老师的手法画成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「曼纳」——曼纳端水时手势很讲究，一举一动都合礼数；记住 manner 是方式、举止，复数 manners 是礼貌。

root: 拉丁语 manus（手）→ 俗拉丁语 manuarius（手的）→ 古法语 maniere（方式、种类）→ 中古英语 maner → 英语 manner。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the shape of a hand's handling; the senses then divide into the way a thing is done, a person's bearing, agreed social politeness and an artist's stroke.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只手握持动作的形状；义项由此分成做事的方式、个人的姿态、社会约定的礼节，以及艺术家的笔法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand holding a cup lightly and a hammer heavily, the pressure never the same.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手，握杯轻、握锤重，落下的力道各不相同。

branches.cn: 落笔前搅动颜料的一只手

branches.en: three sketches of one cup on a long table
branches.cn: 长桌上同一只杯子的三幅画稿

branches.en: a stranger greeted with an easy smile
branches.cn: 用随和笑容迎接陌生人

branches.en: children seated and waiting for the meal
branches.cn: 孩子们坐好等着开饭

branches.en: a painter's repeated stroke on late portraits
branches.cn: 画家在晚期肖像上重复的笔法

intro.en: A Latin noun for hand, a Vulgar Latin adjective of the hand, one French borrowing and three English suffixes carry manner from grip to bearing, politeness and style.
intro.cn: 一个表示「手」的拉丁名词、一个意为「手的」俗拉丁形容词、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 manner 从握持带到姿态、礼貌与风格。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus is recorded and reliable, and the Vulgar Latin adjective manuarius is generally accepted as the bridge to Old French maniere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manus 有记录且可靠，俗拉丁语形容词 manuarius 一般被认为是通向古法语 maniere 的桥。

definition_zh: 许多的；许多（人或物）；许多（后接单数名词）；多数人；大众
definition_en: a large number of countable things; used as a pronoun for a large group; in the pattern many a with a singular noun; and the many as the ordinary majority
core_image: 广场上站满了人，一眼望去数不清有多少张脸
scene: 雨刚停，剧场门口的人已经排成长队，伞还在滴水。By the time the doors opened, many people had already been waiting for hours.
sceneCN: 这里指数目很多的人（第 1 个义项：许多的）；句意为开门时已经有许多人等了几个小时。

pos.zh: 许多的；很多的
许多（人或物）
多数人；大众

derivatives.zh: 由 many 与后缀 -fold（倍）复合，义为「许多倍的；成倍地」
由 many 与 sided 复合，义为「多方面的；多边的」
由 many-sided 加 -ness 构成，义为「多面性」

senses.title: A large number of countable things
senses.definition: used before a plural countable noun to say that the number of things or people is large
senses.definitionCN: 用在可数名词复数前，表示人或物的数目很大
senses.example: Many students walk to the library after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生午饭后步行去图书馆。
senses.why: Old English manig was already an adjective of quantity used with plurals, so the first job of the word is simply to put a large count in front of a noun.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 manig 本来就是与复数连用的数量形容词，所以这个词最初的工作，就是把一个很大的数目放在名词前面。

senses.title: A large number already mentioned
senses.definition: used as a pronoun, usually with of, for a large number of people or things that the listener can identify
senses.definitionCN: 作代词使用，常与 of 连用，指听者能够识别的一大群人或物
senses.example: Many of the old houses were built by the same family.
senses.exampleCN: 这些老房子有许多是同一家人建的。
senses.why: When the noun is dropped, the quantity word has to stand on its own, and of supplies the group it counts; the hearer fills in the rest from context.
senses.whyCN: 名词被省掉后，这个数量词只能自己站住，而 of 引出它所清点的群体；其余部分由听者根据上下文补足。

senses.title: Many a followed by a singular noun
senses.definition: a formal or literary pattern in which many a is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, though the meaning is a large number
senses.definitionCN: 正式或文学性的结构：many a 后接单数名词与单数动词，但表达的是「许多」
senses.example: Many a sailor has told the same story about that storm.
senses.exampleCN: 许多水手都讲过关于那场风暴的同一个故事。
senses.why: The pattern counts one member at a time, which is why the noun and verb stay singular, yet the repetition adds up to a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个结构一次只点一个成员，所以名词和动词都用单数；但一次次相加，最后仍是一个群体。

senses.title: The many as the ordinary majority
senses.definition: the large group of ordinary people, especially when set against a small group with power or wealth
senses.definitionCN: 普通人的大多数，尤指与掌握权力或财富的少数群体相对时
senses.example: The policy was praised by the few and ignored by the many.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策得到少数人称赞，却被多数人忽视。
senses.why: With the definite article, many stops being a count and becomes a name for a social body, the crowd that stands opposite the few.
senses.whyCN: 带上定冠词之后，many 不再清点数量，而成为对一个社会群体的称呼：与少数人相对的众人。

intro.en: Many is a Germanic quantity adjective that has stayed close to its Old English form and keeps company with German manch and Dutch menig.
intro.cn: many 是日耳曼语的数量形容词，形态与古英语时期相距不远，并与德语 manch、荷兰语 menig 同属一族。

items.en: The word appears as manig or monig, an adjective of quantity meaning many or much, used with plural nouns.
items.cn: 这个词写作 manig 或 monig，是表示数量的形容词，意为许多、大量，与复数名词连用。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective *managaz is the common source of the English, German and Dutch forms.
items.cn: 重构形容词 *managaz 是英语、德语与荷兰语诸形式的共同来源。

items.en: Old Norse margr and German manch are cousins, which shows the word was a shared Germanic way of counting a crowd.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 margr 与德语 manch 是近亲，说明这个词是日耳曼语各支共有的清点人群的说法。

items.en: Middle English kept many for plural count nouns and paired it with much for masses, fixing the countable and uncountable split.
items.cn: 中古英语让 many 专管可数名词复数，与管不可数量的 much 配对，固定了可数与不可数的分工。

items.en: Modern English adds the pronoun use with of, the formal pattern many a, and the noun phrase the many for the ordinary majority.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了与 of 连用的代词用法、正式的 many a 结构，以及指普通大众的名词短语 the many。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers quantity words built on or paired with the same Germanic root; the near-meaning group gathers words for a large number.
note.cn: 形近组收同一日耳曼词根上的数量词或与之配对的词；近义组收表示数量众多的词。

entries.definition: The counterpart of many used with uncountable nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 与 many 相对、用于不可数名词的数量词。

entries.definition: The shared comparative of many and much, meaning a larger number or amount.
entries.definitionCN: many 与 much 共同的比较级，表示更多。

entries.definition: The shared superlative of many and much, meaning the largest number or amount.
entries.definitionCN: many 与 much 共同的最高级，表示最多。

entries.definition: Existing in many forms or copies; also a pipe with several branches.
entries.definitionCN: 有多种形式或许多份的；也指多支管的管道。

entries.definition: Existing in large numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 数量众多的，较正式。

entries.definition: Too many to be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 多得数不清的。

entries.definition: More than two but not a large number.
entries.definitionCN: 多于两个但不算很多。

entries.definition: A large amount, enough or more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 大量；充足。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of quantity whose form changed little, and whose grammar splits countable things from masses and from fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是形态变化很小的日耳曼语数量形容词，它的语法把可数事物、不可数总量和固定短语区分开来。

normal.en: Old English manig is the direct ancestor of many, and its -ig ending is the old adjective suffix for having a quality.
normal.cn: 古英语 manig 是 many 的直接祖先，其中的 -ig 词尾就是表示「具有某种性质」的古老形容词后缀。

normal.en: German manch and Dutch menig are cousins of many, which shows the word has been a Germanic quantity term all along.
normal.cn: 德语 manch 与荷兰语 menig 是 many 的近亲，说明这个词一直是日耳曼语的数量词。

normal.en: Many counts separate items and much measures a mass, so the two words divide the countable from the uncountable.
normal.cn: many 清点一件件分开的东西，much 衡量一团总量，两个词由此把可数与不可数分开。

normal.en: More and most are shared with much, which is why many never takes -er or -est.
normal.cn: more 与 most 是和 much 共用的，所以 many 从不加 -er 或 -est。

normal.en: Many a is followed by a singular noun and verb, while many alone takes a plural; the grammar marks the fixed pattern off from ordinary counting.
normal.cn: many a 后接单数名词与单数动词，而单独的 many 接复数；语法把这个固定结构与普通清点区分开来。

abstract.en: A crowd too dense to count is the simplest picture of many: the word begins with the failure of one-by-one counting.
abstract.cn: 一片多到数不清的人群，就是 many 最简单的画面：这个词从「没法一个个数」开始。

abstract.en: Saying many rather than much is a decision about how the world is sliced, into separate things or into a mass.
abstract.cn: 说 many 而不是 much，是在决定世界怎样被切开：切成一件件东西，还是看成一团总量。

abstract.en: The many and the few turn a number word into a picture of society, where counting becomes a question of who holds power.
abstract.cn: the many 与 the few 把一个数词变成社会图景，清点由此变成「谁掌握权力」的问题。

examples.en: Many students walk to the library after lunch.
examples.cn: 许多学生午饭后步行去图书馆。

examples.en: Many of the old houses were built by the same family.
examples.cn: 这些老房子有许多是同一家人建的。

examples.en: Many a sailor has told the same story about that storm.
examples.cn: 许多水手都讲过关于那场风暴的同一个故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「曼妮」——曼妮走到哪儿都有许多人围着；记住 many 是许多。

root: 古英语 manig（许多）一般认为源自原始日耳曼语重构形容词 *managaz；同族词有德语 manch 与荷兰语 menig，无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a large count of separate things; leaving out the noun makes a pronoun, a fixed singular pattern narrows the grammar, and the definite form turns the crowd into a social body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是对一件件可数事物的清点；省略名词后成为代词，固定的单数结构收窄了语法，而定冠形式则把这群人称社会群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square filled with people, too many to count one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上站满了人，多到无法一个个数清。

branches.en: a classroom where most desks are taken

senses.title: A visible spot or line left on a surface
senses.definition: a small area of damage, colour or dirt that shows something has touched or pressed a surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面上一小块颜色、污迹或破损，显示有东西接触或压过
senses.example: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。
senses.why: Old English mearc first named a boundary sign, a visible thing set down to show where something is or has happened, and that visible trace is the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mearc 最初指边界的标志，是一件看得见的东西，用来说明某物在哪里或发生过什么；这种可见的痕迹就是这个词的核心。

senses.title: A written sign or symbol
senses.definition: a sign, symbol or written figure used to represent something or to give information
senses.definitionCN: 用来代表某物或提供信息的符号、记号或书写图样
senses.example: Put a mark beside the name of the candidate you prefer.
senses.exampleCN: 在你更中意的候选人名字旁边做一个标记。
senses.why: Once a visible sign can stand for something other than itself, the boundary trace becomes a symbol, and writing turns that symbol into a small reusable unit of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当一件可见的标记能够代表它自身以外的东西，边界痕迹就变成符号，而文字又把这个符号变成可反复使用的小单位。

senses.title: A score or grade given for work
senses.definition: a number or letter showing how well a piece of schoolwork or a performance has been judged
senses.definitionCN: 表示某份作业或某次表现被评为多好的数字或字母
senses.example: She was pleased with the mark she received on the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的作文分数很满意。
senses.why: A teacher's mark was once a physical sign placed next to an answer; because that sign recorded quality, the sign itself came to mean the judgement written into it.
senses.whyCN: 教师的 mark 原是画在答案旁边的一个实记号；正因为这个记号记录了优劣，记号本身便转而表示写在里面的评判。

senses.title: To leave a visible trace on something
senses.definition: to make a visible spot, line or sign on a surface, often to identify or record something
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上留下可见的点、线或符号，常用来识别或记录
senses.example: She marked the page with a folded corner before returning the book.
senses.exampleCN: 她折了个角给那一页做记号，然后才把书还回去。
senses.why: The verb is the noun put into action: to mark is to produce the very trace that the noun names, and the purpose is usually to make something findable later.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词化为动作：mark 某物，就是造出名词所指的那种痕迹，目的通常是让某样东西日后能被找到。

senses.title: To notice or pay attention to
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, especially because it deserves to be remembered
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，尤因它值得被记住
senses.example: Mark my words: the second attempt will be harder than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 记住我的话：第二次尝试会比第一次更难。
senses.why: A mark draws the eye to one spot, so to mark something in speech is to single it out mentally and ask the listener to keep it in view.
senses.whyCN: 记号把目光引向某一处，所以在言语中说 mark 某事，就是在心里把它单独标出，并要求听者一直记着。

intro.en: Mark began as a Germanic word for a boundary sign, and from that visible sign it grew into a trace, a symbol, a grade and an act of attention.
intro.cn: mark 起初是日耳曼语中表示边界标志的词，从那个可见的标志出发，长出痕迹、符号、分数与注意等义。

items.en: The boundary sense is usually traced to a reconstructed root *merg-, meaning a border or edge, though the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 边界义一般认为可追溯到重构词根 *merg-，意为边界、边缘，但这一重构并不完全确定。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *markō meant a boundary and a sign set on it, and it is the base of the English word.
items.cn: 重构名词 *markō 意为边界以及立在边界上的标志，是英语这个词的词基。

items.en: Old English mearc covered a boundary, a landmark and a sign, so the word already joined the idea of an edge to the idea of something visible.
items.cn: 古英语 mearc 同时表示边界、地标和标志，这个词已经把「边缘」与「看得见的东西」连在一起。

items.en: Middle English mark widened to any trace, target or written symbol, and school use added the sense of a judgement written beside an answer.
items.cn: 中古英语 mark 扩展到任何痕迹、目标或书写符号，学校里的用法又增加了「写在答案旁边的评判」这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb of noticing and the compounds marker, bookmark and trademark, while the border sense survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示「注意」的动词，以及 marker、bookmark、trademark 等复合词，边界义则主要留存在地名里。

core_image: 清晨的集市街：木棚下摆着成筐的果子，一杆秤搁在摊边，买主与卖主在摊前讨价
scene: 天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价。Growers bring their produce to a market where buyers bargain over each crate.
sceneCN: 前半情境：天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价；句中的 market 指「买卖双方定期相聚的集市场地」（第 1 个义项：作为交易场所的集市）。图中可辨识物件：木棚、果筐、杆秤、写价的木牌。

pos.zh: 市场；集市；交易领域；销路；股市；买方群体
行销；推销；把产品推向市场

senses.title: A place where buyers and sellers meet
senses.titleCN: 买卖双方相聚的集市场地
senses.definition: an open place, often with stalls, where people regularly come together to buy and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 常设有摊位的露天场所，人们定期在此相聚买卖货物
senses.example: Farmers set up stalls at the weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每周在集市上摆摊。
senses.why: the Latin noun mercatus named the place and the trading done there, so the word began as a location for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 mercatus 既指场所也指在那里进行的交易，因此这个词最初就是交换的地点。

senses.title: Trade in one particular commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一种商品的交易领域
senses.definition: the whole body of buying and selling in one commodity or one sector, wherever it happens
senses.definitionCN: 某一种商品或某一部门中全部买卖活动的总和，不论发生在何处
senses.example: The world market for copper tightened last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年世界铜的交易领域收紧了。
senses.why: the place sense was transferred from a square to a field of trade, so that copper can have a market with no square at all.
senses.whyCN: 场所义从一方广场转移到一片交易领域，于是铜可以有市场，而完全不需要广场。

senses.title: Demand for a product
senses.definition: the number of buyers willing to purchase something, or the absence of such buyers
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某物的买者数量，或这类买者的缺乏
senses.example: There is little market for hand-written ledgers now.
senses.exampleCN: 如今手写账簿已没什么销路。
senses.why: without buyers a place of exchange is empty, so the word came to mean the willingness to buy rather than the ground it stands on.
senses.whyCN: 没有买主，交换的场所就是空的，于是这个词转而指购买的意愿，而不是它所在的那块地。

senses.title: The market for shares and securities
senses.definition: the organized exchange on which shares, bonds and currencies are traded, or trading there as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 买卖股票、债券与货币的有组织的交易所，或该处的交易整体
senses.example: Share prices fell across the market before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 午前整个股市的股价都下跌了。
senses.why: a stock exchange is a marketplace in the original sense, only with paper claims instead of crates, so the old word was kept.
senses.whyCN: 证券交易所就是原义上的集市，只是货物换成了纸面权益，旧词因此被沿用。

senses.title: Offered for sale
senses.titleCN: 在售；待售（置于售卖状态）
senses.definition: the state of being available to buy, as in a house that has come onto the market
senses.definitionCN: 处于可供购买的状态，如已挂牌出售的房子
senses.example: The building came onto the market in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在春天挂牌出售。
senses.why: being placed before buyers is the modern equivalent of being carried to the stalls, and the phrase on the market keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 被摆到买主面前，相当于旧时把货物挑到摊位上，这一短语保留了那个画面。

senses.title: To sell and promote a product
senses.definition: to promote and sell a product by choosing its buyers, its price and the way it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 通过选择买主、定价与呈现方式来推销并卖出产品
senses.example: The firm markets its software to schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把软件行销给学校。
senses.why: if a market is where goods find buyers, then to market is to do the work of bringing goods and buyers together.
senses.whyCN: 如果市场是货物找到买主的地方，那么行销就是把货物与买主带到一起的工作。

senses.title: The mechanism that sets prices
senses.definition: the system in which prices and quantities are settled by the competing decisions of many buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 价格与数量由众多买卖双方的竞争性决定来敲定的系统
senses.example: The market, not the ministry, decides which suppliers survive.
senses.exampleCN: 决定哪些供应商存活的是市场，而不是部委。
senses.why: abstracting the place away leaves only its function: bringing competing offers together until a price emerges.
senses.whyCN: 把场所抽掉，只剩它的功能：把互相竞争的报价汇集起来，直到价格出现。

senses.title: The body of intended buyers
senses.definition: the group of people or institutions a seller intends to reach, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 卖方打算触及的那一群人或机构，被作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The brand's market is young urban readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的目标买方群体是年轻的城市读者。
senses.why: a seller who studies the crowd at the stalls ends by treating that crowd as an object to be served, which is the marketing sense.
senses.whyCN: 研究摊位前人群的卖方，最终把那群人当作服务对象，这就是营销义。

intro.en: Market is Latin in origin, not a native English word: it goes back to Latin mercatus 'market, trading', a noun from the verb mercari 'to trade', which in turn rests on merx (genitive mercis) 'goods'. It reached Old English through Old Northern French and Germanic channels. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: market 是拉丁来源，而非英语本族词：它上溯至拉丁名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」，该名词出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而动词又基于 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。它经古北法语与日耳曼中介进入古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'goods, merchandise'. Its own deeper origin is uncertain, and no pre-Latin source can be demonstrated.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。它自身更深的来源不确定，无法证明任何拉丁语之前的源头。

items.en: From the noun came the deponent verb mercari 'to buy and sell, to trade', which names the activity rather than the goods.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生异态动词 mercari「买卖、做交易」，命名的是活动而非货物。

items.en: The noun mercatus 'market, marketplace, trading' was formed on the same stem, so place and activity were one word from the start.
items.cn: 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」由同一词干构成，因此场所与活动从一开始就是一个词。

items.en: The form market is generally thought to have come to England through Old Northern French, with Germanic channels also involved in its spread.
items.cn: 一般认为 market 这一形式经古北法语传入英格兰，其传播也涉及日耳曼中介。

items.en: Old English already had market as a loanword, which is why the word counts as Latin in origin rather than as an inherited native term.
items.cn: 古英语已经以借词形式拥有 market，因此这个词算作拉丁来源，而非承继的本族词。

items.en: From the physical fair the word widened to trade in one commodity, to demand, to the share market and finally to the verb for promoting goods.
items.cn: 从有形的集市出发，这个词扩展到单一商品的交易、需求、股票市场，最后扩展到推销货物的动词义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root, so their kinship is real and can be traced; group two holds near neighbours that all name places or gatherings for trade.
note.cn: 第一组的词同出拉丁词根，亲缘关系真实可溯；第二组是同样指交易场所或聚会的近邻词。

entries.definition: Through Old French from Latin mercari: a person who trades, so it shares the root for 'goods' with market and adds an agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自拉丁 mercari：做买卖的人，与本词同出「货物」这一词根，只多了一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: From merx 'goods' through Old French: the goods themselves, which is the root meaning in concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 merx「货物」：货物本身，正是该词根的具体形态。

entries.definition: From Italian mercante, from Latin mercari: relating to trade, a later borrowing of the same root rather than a new coinage.
entries.definitionCN: 经意大利语来自拉丁 mercari：关于贸易的，是同一词根的后期借入，而非新造词。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus merx: trade viewed as an organized exchange between parties, another descendant of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀加 merx：把贸易看作各方之间有组织的交换，是同一词根的另一支后裔。

entries.definition: Market plus place: the square or platform where trading happens, narrower than market because it has no demand or share-price senses.
entries.definitionCN: 由 market 与表示「地方」的成分复合而成：发生交易的广场或平台，比本词窄，因为不含需求与股价等义。

entries.definition: From Latin feria 'holiday': a periodic, often seasonal gathering for trade, with none of the abstract economic senses of market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 feria「节日」：定期、常为季节性的交易聚会，不含本词那些抽象经济义。

entries.definition: From Persian through Turkish: a covered street of shops, a place word only and never a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 经土耳其语来自波斯语：有顶棚的店铺街，只作场所词，从不用作动词。

entries.definition: A shortened form of market kept for names and poetry; it retains only the place sense.
entries.definitionCN: market 的缩略形式，多用于名称与诗歌，只保留场所义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The chain runs goods, then trade, then place: merx, mercari, mercatus.
normal.cn: 链条是货物、交易、场所：merx、mercari、mercatus。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketing, marketplace, marketer, marketable, marketization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 market、marketing、marketplace、marketer、marketable、marketization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: on the market, market share, market forces, stock market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开各个义项：在售、市场份额、市场力量、股票市场。

normal.en: The same root shows in merchant, merchandise, mercantile and commerce.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 merchant、merchandise、mercantile 与 commerce 中。

normal.en: The verb takes an object: to market a product, and the -ing form is the noun marketing.
normal.cn: 动词要带宾语：把产品行销出去，其动名词形式就是名词「营销」。

abstract.en: Picture a square that is crowded at dawn and swept clean by noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一方广场，黎明时挤满人，到正午已被扫空。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: what buyers want, and what they will pay.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上两栏：买主想要什么，愿意付多少。

abstract.en: Picture a board of share prices where one company's fate becomes a single flashing number.
abstract.cn: 想象一块股价牌，一家公司的命运变成一个闪动的数字。

examples.en: The fishing market opens before sunrise and is empty by noon.
examples.cn: 鱼市在日出前开张，到正午便空了。

examples.en: A product with no market cannot survive, however carefully it is made.
examples.cn: 无论做得多用心，没有销路的产品都活不下去。

examples.en: The cooperative markets its coffee directly to roasters abroad.
examples.cn: 这家合作社把咖啡直接行销给国外的烘焙商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马克」的谐音——集市上每件货物都用马克笔标上价钱 → 市场

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ 动词 mercari「做买卖」→ 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」→ 经古北法语与日耳曼中介借入古英语 market；merx 更深来源不确定，故为拉丁来源而非英语本族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one building: goods (merx) are traded (mercari) in a place (mercatus). From the dawn square the line moves to trade in a single commodity, to the demand that fills or empties the square, to the share market that inherited the name, to the state of being offered for sale, to the verb that brings goods and buyers together, to the price-setting mechanism abstracted from the square, and finally to the crowd of buyers a seller sets out to serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座建筑展开：货物在某个场所里被交易。从黎明时的广场出发，这条线依次走向单一商品的交易、决定广场空与满的需求、继承了这个名称的股票市场、被摆出来售卖的状态、把货物与买主带到一起的动词、从广场抽象出来的定价机制，最后走向卖方打算服务的那群买主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dawn market square where crates change hands and the crowd thins by noon.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明的集市广场，成筐货物易手，到正午人群渐散。

branches.en: PLACE AND COMMODITY: a square for exchange becomes a field of trade in one good.
branches.cn: 场所与商品：用于交换的广场变成某一种商品的交易领域。

branches.en: DEMAND AND SHARES: buyers make the square alive, and paper claims inherit its name.
branches.cn: 需求与证券：买主让广场有生气，纸面权益则继承了它的名称。

branches.en: OFFER AND PROMOTE: goods are placed before buyers, and someone must bring them there.
branches.cn: 摆出与推销：货物被摆到买主面前，而总得有人把它们带到那里。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: strip away the square and what remains is a mechanism that settles prices.
branches.cn: 配置：把广场抽走，剩下的就是一个敲定价格的机制。

branches.en: BUYER GROUP: the crowd at the stalls becomes the audience a seller intends to reach.
branches.cn: 买方群体：摊位前的人群变成卖方打算触及的对象。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for 'goods' dressed in noun and verb endings, with English suffixes building the modern family on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是「货物」这一拉丁词根加上名词与动词词尾，再由英语后缀在其上搭起现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx and its verb mercari supply the stem; mercatus, the noun of place and activity, is the direct ancestor of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx 及其动词 mercari 提供词干；指场所与活动的名词 mercatus 则是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of goods in every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为词族中每个成员提供「货物」这一观念。

items.example: Merx names what is carried to the stalls.
items.exampleCN: merx 指被挑到摊位上的东西。

items.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (Latin deponent verb, first conjugation)
items.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell
items.example: The verb turns goods into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把货物变成一种活动。

items.example: The noun carries both the place and the dealing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时承载场所与交易。

items.meaning: a place or system of exchange
items.example: Old English already used the borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已经使用这个借入的名词。

items.example: The compound keeps only the place sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词只保留场所义。

items.example: Marketing grew out of the verb to market.
items.exampleCN: 营销由动词「行销」发展而来。

items.meaning: the process or activity of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a trade activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种行业活动。

items.example: Only marketable varieties reached the stalls.
items.exampleCN: 只有可销售的品种被送上摊位。

items.example: The suffix marks what can be sold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出能够被卖出之物。
